short: The two criteria, approved by the National Science Board, on which NSF judges every proposal.
definition: The pair of criteria, approved by the National Science Board, that NSF applies in merit review to every proposal [157](#cite:157) [160](#cite:160). Five review elements are weighed under each [157](#cite:157). The same two govern awards that follow a person: CAREER proposals and Graduate Research Fellowship applications are reviewed against them [815](#cite:815) [818](#cite:818). In 2025 the National Science Board advised keeping two criteria and pursuing a rename of Broader Impacts to "Societal Benefits", and in December 2025 NSF's mathematical and physical sciences directorate said that its merit-review changes keep the existing criteria [271](#cite:271) [177](#cite:177).

short: The share of applications in a year that receive an award. A funding rate may count something else, such as applicants in place of applications.
definition: The share of applications that receive an award in a fiscal year, as a funder reports it [81](#cite:81). NIH reported a research project grant success rate of 13.0% for FY 2025, from 8,161 new and renewal awards and 62,592 applications, against 18.5% in FY 2024 [81](#cite:81). Its applicant funding rate is a different measure, unique awardees divided by unique applicants on new applications; for early stage investigators on R01-equivalent applications it was 18.9% in FY 2025 [82](#cite:82). NIH publishes success rates by activity code and institute as downloadable report files, with a definition of the term [26](#cite:26). NSF's budget request for FY 2027 shows a research-grant funding rate of 18% in the FY 2025 plan and 7% under the request, which is not enacted [255](#cite:255).

short: A member of a funder's staff who looks after a field or a programme and is the person an applicant asks whether a project fits.
definition: A member of a funding agency's staff who looks after a scientific area or a programme and is named in the funding notice as its contact [120](#cite:120) [158](#cite:158). At NIH, where the title is programme official, such staff can say whether a plan fits their institute and help interpret review feedback, and they do not co-write or edit applications or discuss review details [92](#cite:92) [120](#cite:120). At NSF the programme officer obtains the reviews and makes the recommendation to award or decline; NSF's biology directorate calls the post program director [157](#cite:157) [186](#cite:186). At the Air Force Office of Scientific Research the contact is the programme officer for the research area, while the DOE Office of Science and DARPA say programme manager [339](#cite:339) [281](#cite:281) [343](#cite:343). The "Program Director" in NIH's PD/PI is a different person: the title belongs to the investigator named in the application [12](#cite:12) [4](#cite:4).

short: The agency official responsible for the business side of an award, as distinct from its science: review, negotiation, award and administration.
definition: The official of a funding agency who is responsible for the business management of awards, as distinct from their scientific content [106](#cite:106) [117](#cite:117). NIH's policy statement defines the post as "An NIH official responsible for the business management aspects of grants and cooperative agreements, including review, negotiation, award, and administration." [106](#cite:106) At NIH, grants management officers and specialists handle the business side while programme officials handle the scientific and programmatic side [117](#cite:117) [120](#cite:120) [106](#cite:106). Other agencies have like posts: each SAMHSA notice names a contact in its Division of Grants Management for budget questions, NSF's Division of Grants and Agreements carries out a business review, and in one Labor Department announcement the Grant Officer makes the selection [1112](#cite:1112) [157](#cite:157) [1300](#cite:1300).

short: The person named in an application to lead the project and answer for the conduct of the work. NIH writes PD/PI, for program director/principal investigator.
definition: The individual named in an application to lead the project; in the ordinary case the organisation submits, and the investigator is named in what it submits [4](#cite:4) [815](#cite:815). An IES notice states the duties: the principal investigator has the authority and responsibility for the proper conduct of the research, including the use of federal funds and the submission of progress reports [663](#cite:663). NIH's form of the title is PD/PI, and for an R01 any individual with the skills, knowledge and resources to carry out the research may hold it [4](#cite:4) [117](#cite:117). Since September 25, 2025 NIH accepts six applications per PD/PI per calendar year, for all activity codes except T codes and the R13 [12](#cite:12). Some agencies say project director: NIFA tells the Project Director of an award recommendation, and SAMHSA asks for the project director's eRA Commons username [409](#cite:409) [548](#cite:548).

short: The naming of two or more people to lead one project. NIH speaks of multiple PD/PIs; NSF names a PI and co-PIs.
definition: The naming of more than one person to lead a single project: NIH speaks of multiple PD/PIs, and NSF of a principal investigator with co-PIs [12](#cite:12) [265](#cite:265). Each notice says whether it is allowed: NIH's Transformative Research Award permits multiple PD/PIs, a NIAID programme project notice allows them only for the overall programme leader, and NSF's CAREER and TRAILBLAZER awards go to one investigator with no co-PIs [103](#cite:103) [113](#cite:113) [814](#cite:814) [269](#cite:269). Limits follow the person in either role: NIH's six applications a year count those made as PD/PI or multiple PD/PI, and NSF's SaTC programme caps the proposals on which a person may be PI or co-PI [12](#cite:12) [265](#cite:265). At NIH an application is treated as an early stage investigator application only when every PD/PI on it holds that status [138](#cite:138).

short: The person an organisation authorises to submit applications on its behalf and to sign the certifications that go with them.
definition: The person who holds an organisation's authority to submit a federal application for it [1965](#cite:1965) [548](#cite:548). On Grants.gov it is a role: the E-Business Point of Contact named in SAM.gov holds the Expanded AOR role automatically and assigns roles to others, and an application can be submitted only by a user with the AOR role or an equivalent privilege [1916](#cite:1916) [1895](#cite:1895) [1965](#cite:1965). The holder also certifies for the organisation: at NSF, where the title is Authorized Organizational Representative, that person makes nine certifications with a proposal, among them conflict of interest and responsible and ethical conduct of research [257](#cite:257). Only the Authorized Organizational Representative may submit a proposal through NASA's NSPIRES [1921](#cite:1921). In eRA Commons the like role is the Signing Official, a business official with authority to bind the organisation, whom SAMHSA requires to hold the AOR role in Grants.gov [1911](#cite:1911) [1909](#cite:1909) [548](#cite:548).

short: The office inside an applicant organisation that explains the application process and roles to its researchers and sets up their system accounts.
definition: The office of an applicant organisation to which NIH's help and planning pages send a researcher first: it explains the process and the roles and sets up system accounts [146](#cite:146) [119](#cite:119). System accounts are an example: in eRA Commons the organisation's Signing Official or Account Administrator creates the accounts of PD/PIs and other personnel [1910](#cite:1910) [548](#cite:548). Where a foundation takes only one or a few nominees from an institution, the institution holds an internal competition first, and research offices run that selection [2175](#cite:2175) [2134](#cite:2134). Research offices administer foundation awards that are made to the institution on behalf of a named researcher, and not those paid to the person [2165](#cite:2165). Names vary; NIH's pages say office of sponsored research [146](#cite:146) [119](#cite:119).

short: The legal body that submits an application and, if it succeeds, holds the award. In most federal research funding it is an institution and not a person.
definition: The organisation that submits an application and to which the award is made; the investigator is named in the application and is not the applicant [815](#cite:815) [816](#cite:816) [4](#cite:4). NSF's proposal guide says unaffiliated individuals are not eligible for direct funding, and NIH says the organisations it funds can be domestic or foreign, public or private, non-profit or for-profit [156](#cite:156) [117](#cite:117). Registrations belong to it: for an NIH application the organisation registers in SAM, Grants.gov and eRA Commons [4](#cite:4) [117](#cite:117). Before an award the agency reviews the risk the applicant poses, in an assessment that may weigh financial stability, management systems and audit findings [1809](#cite:1809). Some fellowships depart from the pattern: in NSF's Graduate Research Fellowship the student applies, though the funds are awarded to the institution where the fellow enrols [818](#cite:818).

short: An NIH standing for a lead investigator within 10 years of the final research degree or clinical training who has not yet won a substantial independent NIH research award.
definition: A standing NIH gives to a PD/PI who is within 10 years of the terminal research degree or the end of post-graduate clinical training, whichever is later, and has not yet won a substantial independent NIH research award [138](#cite:138). NIH computes it from the degree date and award history in the investigator's eRA Commons profile, and takes requests to extend it for lapses in research [138](#cite:138). It applies to R01-equivalent applications; every PD/PI on the application must hold it, and NIH says such applications with meritorious scores are prioritised for funding [138](#cite:138). New Investigator is a separate NIH term, for a person who "has not previously competed successfully for Substantial research grants from NIH" [138](#cite:138). In May 2025 NIH extended the status automatically for people whose window ran out during the first half of 2025 [787](#cite:787).

short: A three-character code by which NIH labels each kind of award, such as R01, K08 or T32. The first character usually shows the funding category.
definition: The three-character label NIH gives to each kind of award; the first character usually identifies the funding category, with R for research, T for training, F for fellowship and K for career development [3](#cite:3). A reader meets it in the title of a funding notice, and each parent announcement is for one activity code, such as R01, R21, R03 or R15 [4](#cite:4) [1](#cite:1). Rules attach to codes: each has three standard due dates a year, and NIH's limit of six applications per investigator per calendar year covers all codes except T codes and the R13 [2](#cite:2) [12](#cite:12). One code can serve more than one programme; the Director's Transformative Research Award uses the R01 code under its own yearly notice [103](#cite:103).

short: NIH's code for its research project grant: one defined project, led by a named investigator or investigators, for up to five years.
definition: The NIH activity code for the research project grant, which supports a discrete, specified project carried out by the named investigator or investigators in their area of competence [3](#cite:3). NIH calls it its "most commonly used grant program for independent research projects" [42](#cite:42). Under the parent notice the budget is not capped and the project may run up to five years, and an R01 can be renewed by competing for a further project period [4](#cite:4) [42](#cite:42). New applications have three standard due dates a year and go in through a parent announcement [2](#cite:2) [1](#cite:1). NIH reported an R01-equivalent success rate of 13.0% for FY 2025, against 18.7% for FY 2024, and an average FY 2025 award of $664,005 [81](#cite:81).

short: Two NIH codes for small grants of up to two years: the R21 for exploratory work and the R03 for small projects. Neither can be renewed.
definition: Two NIH activity codes for grants limited in amount and to a project period of two years [5](#cite:5) [6](#cite:6). The R21, the Exploratory/Developmental Research Grant, encourages new research activities: combined direct costs may not exceed $275,000 over the period, with no more than $200,000 in a single year, and preliminary data are not required [3](#cite:3) [5](#cite:5) [43](#cite:43). The R03, the Small Research Grant, allows $50,000 in direct costs a year for uses such as pilot studies, secondary analysis of existing data and development of methods or technology [6](#cite:6) [44](#cite:44). Neither can be renewed, and in both the research strategy is limited to 6 pages [43](#cite:43) [44](#cite:44). Not all NIH institutes and centers take part in every parent announcement [43](#cite:43).

short: NIH's code for research grants to institutions that have had little NIH support: AREA for undergraduate-focused ones, REAP for health professional and graduate schools.
definition: The NIH activity code for small-scale research projects at educational institutions that train many of the nation's research scientists but have not been major recipients of NIH support [3](#cite:3). It has two versions: AREA, for undergraduate-focused institutions, and REAP, for health professional schools and graduate schools [7](#cite:7) [8](#cite:8). In both the institution must not have received NIH support of more than $6 million per year in 4 of the last 7 years, and an award is up to $375,000 in direct costs for a project of up to three years [7](#cite:7) [8](#cite:8). NIH states three goals: to support meritorious research, expose students to research and strengthen the institution's research environment [45](#cite:45). The PD/PI may not lead an active NIH research grant and may hold only one R15 at a time [7](#cite:7) [45](#cite:45).

short: NIH's code for a research project funded as a cooperative agreement, in which NIH staff take part in the work after the award is made.
definition: The NIH activity code for a research project cooperative agreement: the same kind of discrete research project as the R01, funded under a cooperative agreement instead of a grant [49](#cite:49) [3](#cite:3). What marks a cooperative agreement off from a grant is that substantial involvement is expected between the agency and the recipient while the work is carried out [1851](#cite:1851). A NIAID notice puts it so: "After award, NIH scientific or program staff will assist, guide, coordinate, or participate in project activities." [116](#cite:116) The terms of each notice name the NIH roles and a dispute panel [116](#cite:116). There is no parent U01; a search of Grants.gov on October 4, 2026 returned 33 open notices, each for a defined programme, and NIH's simplified review framework lists other codes that begin with U beside it, among them U34, UG3 and UH3 [111](#cite:111) [41](#cite:41).

short: NIH's code for a one-year grant that buys a research instrument for a group of NIH-funded investigators to share. It pays no indirect costs.
definition: The NIH activity code for instrumentation grants, which buy a commercially available research instrument, or an integrated system, for NIH-funded investigators to share [1534](#cite:1534) [1536](#cite:1536). The Shared Instrumentation Grant notice posted June 25, 2026 consolidates the former Shared, High-End and Basic Instrumentation Grant programmes; awards run from $300,000 to $5,000,000 for one year, and the application names at least three NIH-funded Major Users [1536](#cite:1536). A second notice, Seed Instrumentation Support, covers a single instrument costing $50,000 to $400,000 and asks for at least two NIH-funded users, at least one of them from the applicant institution [1537](#cite:1537). S10 awards do not allow indirect costs, and neither notice requires cost sharing [1536](#cite:1536) [1537](#cite:1537). NIH's Office of Research Infrastructure Programs runs the programmes through its Division of Construction and Instruments [1538](#cite:1538).

short: An NIH award that gives a named researcher salary and research support, with protected time, to develop a research career. The institution applies for the candidate.
definition: An NIH award in the K series of activity codes that gives a named candidate salary and research support, with protected time, for career development; the applicant is the candidate's institution [744](#cite:744) [3](#cite:3). In the mentored awards, such as the K01, K08 and K23, the candidate works under a mentor and commits at least 75 percent of full-time professional effort, and the project period may not exceed 5 years [744](#cite:744) [745](#cite:745) [746](#cite:746). Each participating institute sets its own salary and research support levels, and indirect costs are reimbursed at 8% of modified total direct costs [744](#cite:744). The K99/R00 joins up to 2 years of mentored support to up to 3 years of independent research support for a postdoctoral researcher moving to a faculty post [743](#cite:743). NIH announced on August 12, 2026 that for due dates on or after October 12, 2027 most individual K codes are replaced by four: KR1, KC1, KS1 and KT1/R00 [742](#cite:742).

short: An NIH fellowship for one named doctoral student or postdoctoral researcher, who trains under a sponsor. It pays a stipend and allowances, and no indirect costs.
definition: A fellowship in NIH's F series of activity codes that supports one named person's mentored research training under a faculty sponsor; it is one of the Kirschstein National Research Service Awards [736](#cite:736) [737](#cite:737). The F31 is for doctoral students, the F30 for students in a combined MD/PhD or other dual-doctoral degree programme, and the F32 for postdoctoral researchers [736](#cite:736) [738](#cite:738) [737](#cite:737). The applicant organisation submits the application, and by the time of award the candidate must be a citizen or non-citizen national of the United States, or lawfully admitted for permanent residence [784](#cite:784) [736](#cite:736). The award pays a stipend, a contribution to tuition and fees and an institutional allowance, with no separate payment for indirect costs [736](#cite:736). Applications are scored on three criteria, which replaced five for due dates on or after January 25, 2025 [736](#cite:736) [794](#cite:794).

short: An NIH grant to an institution to run a research training programme. The institution, not NIH, selects the trainees, who receive NRSA stipends.
definition: An NIH award made to an institution to run a research training programme for a group of predoctoral students, postdoctoral researchers or both [750](#cite:750). The institution applies through a programme director, then selects and appoints the trainees, who receive NRSA stipends; a student or postdoctoral researcher does not apply to NIH for a place [750](#cite:750) [730](#cite:730). Project periods run up to five years and are renewable, and application budgets are not limited [750](#cite:750). Eligible organisations are domestic, and a trainee must be a citizen or noncitizen national of the United States, or lawfully admitted for permanent residence, at the time of appointment [750](#cite:750). Indirect costs are reimbursed at 8% of modified total direct costs, a base that leaves out tuition and fees, consortium costs in excess of $25,000 and equipment [750](#cite:750).

short: The family of NIH research training awards, named for Ruth L. Kirschstein, that pay a stipend to a student or postdoctoral researcher on a fellowship or a training grant.
definition: NIH's family of research training awards that pay a stipend as a subsistence allowance; the full name adds Ruth L. Kirschstein [736](#cite:736). They come as individual fellowships, such as the F31 and F32, and as trainee places on institutional training grants, such as the T32 [736](#cite:736) [737](#cite:737) [750](#cite:750). To hold one a person must be a citizen or a non-citizen national of the United States, or lawfully admitted for permanent residence [736](#cite:736) [750](#cite:750). Support is limited in aggregate to 5 years at the predoctoral level, 6 for dual-degree training, and to 3 years at the postdoctoral level, counting training grant appointments and individual fellowships together [736](#cite:736) [737](#cite:737). NIH sets the stipend levels once a fiscal year in a notice, and the first 12 months of postdoctoral support bring a service payback obligation [732](#cite:732) [737](#cite:737).

short: NSF's five-year award for untenured, tenure-track faculty who combine research and education. The employing organisation submits for one investigator.
definition: A five-year NSF award for early-career faculty who combine research and education; the programme's full name is the Faculty Early Career Development Program [814](#cite:814). The employing organisation submits the proposal on behalf of one investigator, and co-investigators are not allowed [815](#cite:815) [816](#cite:816). The investigator must hold a doctoral degree and at least a 50% tenure-track or equivalent post as an assistant professor or equivalent, be untenured, and may submit one proposal per annual competition in no more than three competitions [815](#cite:815). The award has a floor and no ceiling: at least $400,000 over five years including indirect costs, and at least $500,000 in BIO, ENG and the Office of Polar Programs [815](#cite:815) [816](#cite:816). NSF chooses its nominees for the Presidential Early Career Awards for Scientists and Engineers from recent CAREER awardees [814](#cite:814).

short: An NSF fellowship that gives a graduate student three years of support for a research-based degree in a STEM field. The student applies directly to NSF.
definition: An NSF fellowship that gives a graduate student three years of support, to be used within a five-year fellowship period, for a research-based master's or doctoral degree in a STEM field [818](#cite:818) [817](#cite:817). The student applies directly to NSF; the funds are awarded to the institution where the fellow enrols, and there is no post-graduate service requirement [818](#cite:818) [819](#cite:819). A year of support is a $37,000 stipend and a $16,000 cost-of-education allowance paid to the institution [817](#cite:817) [818](#cite:818). Under the solicitation for the FY 2027 competition an applicant must be a U.S. citizen, national or permanent resident, a graduate student may apply only once, in the first year of the first graduate programme, and second-year graduate students are not eligible [818](#cite:818). The FY 2027 budget request, which is not enacted, asks for $246.54 million for the programme against $433.00 million in the FY 2025 current plan [255](#cite:255).

short: Two NSF proposal types: EAGER for early exploratory work on untested ideas, RAPID for time-sensitive work. Each starts with a concept outline to the programme officer.
definition: Two types of proposal defined in Chapter II.F of NSF's proposal guide, the PAPPG: EAGER for exploratory work in its early stages on untested but potentially transformative research ideas, and RAPID for time-sensitive work [257](#cite:257) [251](#cite:251) [212](#cite:212). The investigator first sends a concept outline to the programme director, and a full proposal follows once NSF allows it [166](#cite:166) [185](#cite:185). Since December 8, 2025 a request may be for up to $400,000 over up to two years for EAGER and up to $300,000 over up to one year for RAPID, indirect costs included; the ceilings before were $300,000 and $200,000 [149](#cite:149). NSF's early-career page says EAGER proposals are reviewed internally, and a declined EAGER or RAPID proposal is not eligible for reconsideration [251](#cite:251) [258](#cite:258). NSF proposed on June 24, 2026 to replace the PAPPG with a Guidance on Financial Assistance, which it aims to issue for use in early to mid FY2027 [152](#cite:152) [151](#cite:151).

short: A fixed sum paid to a fellow or trainee to live on during training, at a level the funder sets.
definition: A payment made to a fellow or trainee as a subsistence allowance during training [736](#cite:736). NIH sets NRSA stipends once a fiscal year: for awards made with FY 2026 funds the level is $29,364 a year for predoctoral trainees and fellows and from $63,480 to $77,076 for postdoctoral ones, by years of experience, and earlier awards are not adjusted [732]. NSF's Graduate Research Fellowship carries a stipend of $37,000 for a 12-month tenure period, paid by the fellow's institution [818](#cite:818). Sums for the institution come beside it, such as a contribution to tuition and fees and an institutional or cost-of-education allowance [736](#cite:736) [818](#cite:818). An NRSA fellowship may not be held together with another federally sponsored fellowship or similar federal award that provides a stipend [737](#cite:737).

short: A fixed yearly sum paid to the institution that hosts a fellow, for costs such as health insurance, supplies and administration. A fellowship that pays one often pays no indirect costs.
definition: A fixed sum paid with a fellowship to the fellow's institution to meet the costs of hosting and administering it, where no indirect costs are paid [736](#cite:736) [960](#cite:960). On an NIH individual fellowship it covers health insurance, supplies, equipment, books and travel; for FY 2026 it is $4,750 predoctoral and $12,400 postdoctoral, or $3,650 and $11,300 for fellows at federal and for-profit institutions [732](#cite:732) [736](#cite:736). NIH training grants carry training-related expenses in its place, at $4,750 and $12,400 as well [732](#cite:732). NIFA's AFRI predoctoral and postdoctoral fellowships pay the institution $3,000 a year and do not permit indirect costs [960]. NSF's counterpart is the cost-of-education allowance, $16,000 per tenure year in the Graduate Research Fellowship, for which the institution must exempt the fellow from tuition and required fees [818](#cite:818).

short: A condition of some training awards and scholarships: the recipient owes a period of qualifying work afterwards, or may have to repay the money.
definition: A duty attached to some awards made for a person's training: to do a set period of qualifying work afterwards, or to repay [769](#cite:769) [919](#cite:919). Under NIH's NRSA the first 12 months of postdoctoral support bring a payback obligation, discharged by an equal number of months of further postdoctoral NRSA support or of health-related research, research training or teaching averaging at least 20 hours a week, begun within 2 years of the end of support [737](#cite:737) [769](#cite:769). A signed Payback Agreement Form (PHS 6031) accompanies the activation notice, and NIH may extend the time, waive the obligation or require repayment with interest within 3 years [737](#cite:737) [769](#cite:769). The defence SMART scholarship leads to civilian employment at a department facility, and a 2019 Federal Register document set the period owed at the period of degree study covered [917](#cite:917) [919](#cite:919). NSF's Graduate Research Fellowship has no post-graduate service requirement [819](#cite:819).

short: A programme that pays down a person's educational debt in return for a period of qualifying work, such as research or teaching. The person applies, not the employer.
definition: A programme that pays down part of a person's educational debt in return for a period of work [762](#cite:762) [763](#cite:763) [1033](#cite:1033). NIH's Extramural Loan Repayment Program repays up to $50,000 of qualified educational debt a year, under a two-year award that can be renewed, for health professionals who do research outside NIH for at least 20 hours a week [762] [763]. The individual applies and the employer does not receive the award; the debt must be at least 20 percent of institutional base salary, the research must be supported by a domestic non-profit institution or a U.S. government agency, and NIH research funding is not required [762]. For the cycle that opened on September 1, 2026 NIH has three subcategories, coded L30, L40 and L70, after a consolidation [762] [765] [1085]. HRSA's Faculty Loan Repayment Program repays up to $40,000 over two years in return for service on the faculty of an approved health professions school [1033](#cite:1033).

short: The identifier SAM.gov assigns to an organisation. Every federal application carries it, and a subrecipient needs one before a subaward can be made.
definition: The identifier that SAM.gov assigns to an organisation; 2 CFR 25.400 defines it as "the universal identifier assigned by SAM.gov to uniquely identify an entity" [1899](#cite:1899). It replaced the DUNS number on April 4, 2022 [1969](#cite:1969) [1909](#cite:1909). Every applicant includes it in each application, and a subrecipient must have one before a subaward can be made [1899](#cite:1899) [1900](#cite:1900). An organisation can get the identifier alone, by giving its legal business name and physical address, but with that alone it cannot apply directly for federal awards; a prime applicant needs the full SAM.gov registration, which also assigns the identifier [1897](#cite:1897). SAM.gov makes no charge for it, and the same one is used in every later registration, such as Grants.gov and eRA Commons [1898](#cite:1898) [784](#cite:784).

short: The federal registry, run by the General Services Administration, in which an organisation holds an active registration before it applies for federal grant money in its own name.
definition: The federal registry, run by the General Services Administration, in which an organisation holds an active entity registration before it applies for federal financial assistance as a prime awardee [1897](#cite:1897) [1899](#cite:1899). Registration assigns the Unique Entity ID and, for a domestic organisation, a CAGE code; an entity may register for financial assistance awards only, which asks for less than a registration for all awards [1898](#cite:1898) [784](#cite:784). SAM.gov states that registering is free, that a registration can take up to 10 business days to become active and that it is renewed every 365 days; NIH says to allow three weeks or more for a first registration [1898](#cite:1898) [1897](#cite:1897) [1909](#cite:1909). A subrecipient needs only a Unique Entity ID [1900](#cite:1900). Since March 8, 2025 subaward reports have been made in SAM.gov too, and on January 28, 2026 GSA proposed, for comment until March 30, 2026, to update the financial assistance certifications made there, stating no effective date [1903](#cite:1903) [1866](#cite:1866).

short: A Commercial and Government Entity code, given to a domestic organisation as part of its SAM.gov registration. A foreign organisation obtains an NCAGE code first.
definition: A Commercial and Government Entity code, which a domestic organisation is assigned as part of SAM registration, for grants as for contracts [784](#cite:784) [1898](#cite:1898). A U.S. entity that has none answers 'No' in the registration, and one is assigned and then validated [1898](#cite:1898). An organisation outside the United States obtains a NATO Commercial and Government Entity (NCAGE) code in its place, requested through the NCAGE Request Tool before the SAM.gov registration is started [784](#cite:784) [1898](#cite:1898). CDMRP says SAM.gov registration takes several weeks, including 10-15 business days to process a CAGE code request or UEI renewal [1923](#cite:1923). The ONR and AFOSR announcements read list the code among their required registrations [334](#cite:334) [339](#cite:339).

short: The person an organisation names in its SAM.gov registration as its contact for electronic business. That person controls who may act for the organisation in Grants.gov.
definition: The person an organisation names in its SAM.gov registration as its Electronic Business contact, one of the mandatory points of contact there, with Accounts Receivable and Government Business [1898](#cite:1898) [1895](#cite:1895). Grants.gov tells that person to use the same email address in both systems, because the contact named in SAM.gov holds the Expanded AOR role in Grants.gov automatically and assigns roles to colleagues [1895](#cite:1895) [1965](#cite:1965). Other systems rest on the same entry: FEMA GO makes the person listed there its primary Authorized Organization Representative, matched by email address, and NASA's guidebook requires the contact to be registered in SAM.gov [1959](#cite:1959) [1921](#cite:1921). SAM.gov also has an entity administrator, the person who registers and renews the organisation there [1909](#cite:1909).

short: The federal website where most agencies post funding opportunities and receive applications.
definition: The federal site where most agencies post funding opportunities and receive applications [1895](#cite:1895). An organisation registers there after SAM.gov, using its Unique Entity ID; the person named in SAM.gov as Electronic Business Point of Contact assigns roles, and a user with an Authorized Organization Representative role or an equivalent privilege submits [1895](#cite:1895) [1965](#cite:1965). Applications are prepared and submitted in Workspace, and every user signs in with a Login.gov account [1915](#cite:1915) [1965](#cite:1965). A person applying on their own behalf adds an Individual Applicant profile and does not register with SAM.gov [1896](#cite:1896). Since December 23, 2025 the default search for opportunities has been on Simpler.Grants.gov, the site on which HHS is building the next generation of Grants.gov; its roadmap announces 2027 as the stage at which it replaces the legacy site, with no day or month given [1920](#cite:1920) [1967](#cite:1967) [1919](#cite:1919).

short: The shared space in Grants.gov where a team fills in the forms of one application package before an authorised person submits it.
definition: The shared space in Grants.gov in which members of a team fill in the forms of one application package, online or as downloaded PDFs, before a user with an Authorized Organization Representative (AOR) role submits it [1915](#cite:1915) [1965](#cite:1965). Grants.gov calls it the standard way for organisations or individuals to apply [1915](#cite:1915). A Workspace Manager, the minimum role needed to create a workspace, may not submit, while a Standard AOR may create workspaces and submit [1916](#cite:1916) [1965](#cite:1965). An application can be submitted when all required forms are complete and pass error checks, the organisation's SAM.gov registration is active and the deadline has not passed; submitted packages are kept for 5 years [1965](#cite:1965) [1966](#cite:1966). The Simpler.Grants.gov roadmap lists a simpler application workflow under test with partner agencies, and that site's home page says a user may need to visit Grants.gov to apply for most opportunities [1919](#cite:1919) [1967](#cite:1967).

short: The NIH-run system in which an applicant organisation and its people hold accounts for applications, awards and reports. Several other agencies use it as well.
definition: The system, run by NIH's electronic Research Administration (eRA), in which an applicant organisation and its people hold accounts for applications, awards and reports [1911](#cite:1911) [1910](#cite:1910). The agencies eRA lists as supported include NIH, FDA, CDC, SAMHSA, AHRQ, the National Institute of Food and Agriculture and the Department of Defense [1913](#cite:1913). A Signing Official, a business official with authority to bind the organisation, registers it once, after SAM.gov registration; that official or an Account Administrator then creates an account for each PD/PI, senior/key person and other significant contributor named on an application or award [1911](#cite:1911) [1909](#cite:1909) [1910](#cite:1910). NIH says to allow two weeks or more for this registration and six weeks or more for the whole set [1909](#cite:1909). Users sign in with two-factor authentication through Login.gov or an InCommon federated account, and for due dates on or after January 25, 2026 each person who submits a Common Form links an ORCID iD to the eRA Commons profile [1911](#cite:1911) [1914](#cite:1914) [31](#cite:31).

short: The eRA module in which an application is prepared online, checked for errors and sent on through Grants.gov.
definition: The eRA module for preparing an application on the SF-424 forms, checking it and sending it through Grants.gov [548](#cite:548). NIH's fellowship notices name it as one of three routes to Grants.gov, with an institutional system-to-system solution and Grants.gov Workspace [784](#cite:784). A user signs in with the eRA Commons ID received at registration, runs the 'Validate Application' function and submits once errors are cleared; the application is then followed under 'View Submission Status Details' [548](#cite:548). SAMHSA advises its applicants to prepare the application in it, with Grants.gov Workspace as the other route, and NIH loan repayment applications are submitted in it [548](#cite:548) [763](#cite:763).

short: The National Science Foundation's own system for preparing and submitting proposals and for filing reports after an award.
definition: NSF's system for preparing and submitting proposals and for reports after award [161](#cite:161) [1955](#cite:1955). An organisation registers there, holding an active SAM registration and a Unique Entity ID first, and each person holds one NSF ID, the identifier NSF assigns to a user [161](#cite:161) [156](#cite:156). A proposal may instead be sent through Grants.gov, after which it passes to Research.gov for processing; a subrecipient named in a proposal obtains a UEI and registers in Research.gov without needing a SAM registration [161](#cite:161) [156](#cite:156). Multifactor authentication has been required at every sign-in since October 27, 2024, with NSF, Login.gov or organisation-issued InCommon credentials, and from April 26, 2025 users must verify that their NSF primary email address matches their Login.gov address [1971](#cite:1971) [1972](#cite:1972). NSF gives no figure for the registration itself and advises beginning SAM registration at least 90 days before submission [161](#cite:161).

short: NASA's system for grant proposals before award. The organisation and every person with a role in a proposal register in it.
definition: NASA's pre-award system for grant proposals [1947](#cite:1947). NASA's guidebook for unsolicited proposals states that every organisation that intends to submit must be registered in it, and so must every individual with a role in the proposed work, who also confirms that role [1921](#cite:1921). Only the organisation's Authorized Organizational Representative may submit a proposal through it [1921](#cite:1921). The principal investigator must be a registered user even when the proposal is sent through Grants.gov [389](#cite:389). From September 1, 2026 NASA accepts the biographical sketch and current and pending (other) support forms of senior/key persons only as NASA-specific forms prepared in SciENcv [1946](#cite:1946).

short: The Department of Justice system in which the full grant application is submitted and awards are managed.
definition: The Department of Justice's grants management system, used by the Office of Justice Programs, the COPS Office and the Office on Violence Against Women [618](#cite:618). An application is made in two steps: the SF-424 goes through Grants.gov, and the full application is then submitted in JustGrants by a second deadline [619](#cite:619). After the SF-424 is in, DOJ emails instructions for creating an account, which it expects to send within 24 hours, and the applicant's Entity Administrator manages which users may act for it [619](#cite:619). DOJ urges finishing each step at least 48 hours before its deadline, and requires an active SAM.gov registration of every entity seeking its grant funding [619](#cite:619) [618](#cite:618). Awards are managed in the same system, while payment requests are made in Treasury's ASAP system [619](#cite:619) [1924](#cite:1924).

short: A web-based grants management system that some federal agencies use to issue and manage awards. Recipients see the Notice of Award in it and file requests and reports.
definition: A web-based grants management system in which some federal agencies and their recipients manage awards [1961](#cite:1961) [1962](#cite:1962). ACF and its recipients use it for discretionary and non-discretionary awards, and CDC uses its Grants Management Module for CDC/ATSDR grants and cooperative agreements [1961](#cite:1961) [1962](#cite:1962). Recipients see the Notice of Award there and file post-award requests and programme reports; its Online Data Collection system (OLDC) takes real property, financial and performance reports and needs a separate access form [1961](#cite:1961). An ACF recipient asks for an account with a Recipient User Account Request form, signed by a supervisor or authorized official [1961](#cite:1961). A Department of Education release of March 17, 2026 says awards in the first competition under the Education-Labor postsecondary partnership are issued on the Department of Labor's GrantSolutions platform [1015](#cite:1015).

short: The Health Resources and Services Administration's own grants system. Some HRSA notices need a second submission in it after Grants.gov, and recipients file progress reports there.
definition: HRSA's own grants system, reached at grants.hrsa.gov [1927](#cite:1927). Members of an applicant or grantee organisation register once, choose a role (Authorizing Official, Business Official or Other) and are tied to the organisation's record once its Primary Authorizing Official approves the request [1927](#cite:1927). A notice submitted in two phases goes first to Grants.gov and then to the EHBs, and progress reports are filed there after award [1194](#cite:1194). Since August 28, 2025 outside users have signed in with an identity-verified Login.gov or ID.me account and two-factor authentication [1926](#cite:1926). HRSA's page on mandatory registrations before applying names SAM and Grants.gov only [1925](#cite:1925).

short: The DOE Office of Science system in which letters of intent and pre-applications are submitted. The application itself goes through Grants.gov.
definition: The Portfolio Analysis and Management System, in which letters of intent and pre-applications to the DOE Office of Science are submitted, alongside Grants.gov for the application itself [279](#cite:279) [1922](#cite:1922). The principal investigator, and anyone submitting on the PI's behalf, registers for an account; the FY 2027 annual notice encourages doing so at least a week in advance [279](#cite:279). A new user first logs in through DOE's OneID, and international users are encouraged to use Login.gov [1922](#cite:1922). The public site also offers a search of awards and a search of solicitations [1922](#cite:1922).

short: The portal of the Congressionally Directed Medical Research Programs, where the pre-application that every one of its funding opportunities requires is submitted.
definition: The Electronic Biomedical Research Application Portal, the portal of the Congressionally Directed Medical Research Programs (CDMRP) [358](#cite:358) [1923](#cite:1923). Every CDMRP funding opportunity requires a pre-application there: a letter of intent, which is not reviewed, or a pre-proposal, which is reviewed and leads to an invitation or not [1923](#cite:1923). Extramural organisations then submit the full application through Grants.gov, intramural Department of Defense organisations submit it through eBRAP, and the applicant checks the application in eBRAP during a verification period [1923](#cite:1923). Investigators and organisations both register, and the organisation profile carries the UEI from SAM.gov; CDMRP states that PI registration is processed immediately and organisation registration takes 1-2 days with a UEI [358](#cite:358) [1923](#cite:1923). CDMRP also states that there are no grace periods for deadlines [1923](#cite:1923).

short: The online system in which recipients of NEH and IMLS awards manage them after award: reports, requests for changes and messages to the agency.
definition: The online award management system used by recipients and reviewers at two agencies, NEH and IMLS [1932](#cite:1932) [1960](#cite:1960). NEH describes it as the system its panelists and recipients use for all award management activities, among them prior approval and extension requests, reports and messages to NEH staff [1932](#cite:1932). At IMLS, which brought in eGMS as its grants management system on October 1, 2019, awardees view award information there and submit performance reports, interim and final financial reports, payment requests and change requests [1933](#cite:1933) [1960](#cite:1960). Since January 20, 2023 each user at either agency has signed in through a Login.gov account tied to the email address the agency holds, and NEH does not allow shared accounts [1932](#cite:1932) [1960](#cite:1960).

short: The Department of Education's grants and financial management system, which replaced G5 in 2023. Grantees draw down payments in it.
definition: The Department of Education's grants and financial management system, at g6.ed.gov [1963](#cite:1963). It replaced G5 (g5.gov) in a change completed on October 30, 2023, and users sign in with Login.gov or with existing G5 credentials [1963](#cite:1963). Grantees draw down payments in it [1964](#cite:1964). Applying is a separate matter: under the Department's common instructions of August 29, 2025, applications for discretionary grants are submitted through Grants.gov, and those instructions do not mention G5 or G6 [1928](#cite:1928). An earlier notice, for the fiscal year 2025 Fulbright-Hays dissertation fellowships, required electronic submission in G6 [1012](#cite:1012).

short: The Federal Emergency Management Agency's grants management system, used to apply for, track and manage its grants.
definition: FEMA Grants Outcomes, the grants management system of the Federal Emergency Management Agency, used to apply for, track and manage its grants [1957](#cite:1957). It draws the organisation's record from SAM.gov, so the organisation needs an active SAM.gov registration with a UEI [1958](#cite:1958) [1959](#cite:1959). The person listed in SAM.gov as Electronic Business point of contact registers with the same email address and becomes the primary Authorized Organization Representative, who adds team members and gives each a role; a Grant Writer may draft and cannot submit [1959](#cite:1959). Not every applicant uses it: for the Nonprofit Security Grant Program only the State Administrative Agency applies in FEMA GO, and a non-profit submits to that state agency [1320](#cite:1320).

short: The Department of Agriculture's online system for applying for and managing USDA grants and agreements.
definition: USDA's online system for applying for and managing its grants and agreements, described by the department's Office of the Chief Financial Officer as its system of record for financial assistance transactions [1929](#cite:1929). The page lists agency contacts for AMS, APHIS, FAS, NIFA, NRCS and OPPE [1929](#cite:1929). Access takes a Login.gov account linked to USDA eAuthentication, a verified identity (online through Login.gov or in person at a USDA Service Center) and a requested user role [1929](#cite:1929). Not every USDA application goes through it: NIFA's own how-to-apply page directs applications to Grants.gov [1930](#cite:1930).

short: The Department of Housing and Urban Development's electronic system for Continuum of Care applications and grants management.
definition: The electronic application and grants management system of the Continuum of Care (CoC) Program, used by HUD's Office of Special Needs Assistance Programs [1935](#cite:1935). Collaborative Applicants file the CoC consolidated application and the project priority listing in it, and project applicants file project applications [1935](#cite:1935). Each person creates an individual user profile and then asks the administrator of the organisation's or the CoC's account for access to it [1935](#cite:1935).

short: A federal sign-in service that lets one personal account open many government websites, among them most of the grant systems.
definition: A sign-in service, provided by GSA's Technology Transformation Services, that lets one account open many federal sites [1953](#cite:1953). It is the sign-in for SAM.gov, Grants.gov, Simpler.Grants.gov, the Federal Audit Clearinghouse, iEdison, eGMS Reach and ezFedGrants, and one of the accepted sign-ins for eRA Commons, Research.gov, HRSA's Electronic Handbooks and the Department of Education's G6 [1897](#cite:1897) [1965](#cite:1965) [1967](#cite:1967) [1881](#cite:1881) [1951](#cite:1951) [1932](#cite:1932) [1960](#cite:1960) [1929](#cite:1929) [1911](#cite:1911) [1971](#cite:1971) [1926](#cite:1926) [1963](#cite:1963). An account belongs to a person, not to an organisation, and several systems require its email address to match the address on the system account [1932](#cite:1932) [1972](#cite:1972) [1960](#cite:1960) [1951](#cite:1951) [1926](#cite:1926). Creating one takes an email address, a password of at least 12 characters and an authentication method; where a system asks for it, the person also verifies identity with a photo ID [1977](#cite:1977) [1953](#cite:1953). Between 2023 and 2026 the grant systems moved from their own passwords to Login.gov or another verified credential with a second factor, each on its own date [1971](#cite:1971) [1926](#cite:1926) [1932](#cite:1932).

short: A shared service of the Department of Health and Human Services that pays out grant funds for federal agencies. Recipients draw down money and file financial reports in it.
definition: A shared service, run by the HHS Program Support Center, that pays grant funds for federal agencies [1936](#cite:1936). Recipients draw down funds in it and file the Federal Financial Report (SF-425) [1961](#cite:1961). The pages read name ACF and NASA among the agencies that pay through it, and HRSA recipients send it the yearly Federal Financial Report [1961](#cite:1961) [1947](#cite:1947) [1194](#cite:1194). Each user requests access online, with ID.me as the partner system; the user's supervisor verifies the request, the Program Support Center reviews it, and requests are processed within four business days [1973](#cite:1973) [1974](#cite:1974). A user who does not log in once every 60 days has the access deactivated [1973](#cite:1973).

short: The Treasury system through which some federal agencies pay grant money to recipient organisations. The paying agency, not the recipient, starts the enrolment.
definition: The Treasury system through which federal agencies transfer money to recipient organisations [1937](#cite:1937). NIFA describes it as a secure web-based payment and information system built by Treasury's Bureau of the Fiscal Service and the Federal Reserve Bank of Kansas City [1931](#cite:1931). The paying agency enrols the recipient, authorises its payments and manages its account, so enrolment begins only when the agency sends an invitation [1937](#cite:1937) [1956](#cite:1956). The recipient's Point of Contact then confirms the organisation's details and names the other officials, the Authorizing Official names the users, and the Financial Official enters the bank account information [1956](#cite:1956). NIFA awardees and DOJ recipients are paid through it, and it is free for agencies and recipient organisations [1931](#cite:1931) [1924](#cite:1924) [1937](#cite:1937).

short: A persistent identifier for an individual researcher, free to the researcher. NIH requires one of every person who submits a Common Form.
definition: A persistent identifier for a researcher, issued by ORCID, a global not-for-profit organisation sustained by fees from member organisations [1950](#cite:1950). Researchers create, edit and maintain the identifier and its record free of charge [1950](#cite:1950). NIH requires one of every person who submits a Biographical Sketch or Current and Pending (Other) Support Common Form, linked to that person's eRA Commons account, for due dates and for JIT, RPPR and prior approval submissions on or after January 25, 2026 [31](#cite:31). DOE requires a persistent identifier field on notices and awards that include research and development, and its annual Office of Science notice asks for each senior/key person's ORCID iD if known [1944](#cite:1944) [279](#cite:279). It is also one of the credentials with which a person can sign in to SciENcv [1980](#cite:1980).

short: A researcher profile system, run by NCBI at the National Library of Medicine, in which the federal biographical sketch and current and pending support forms are produced.
definition: A researcher profile system, run by NCBI at the National Library of Medicine, for individuals who apply for, receive or are associated with research investments from federal agencies [1943](#cite:1943). It is the tool in which the two government-wide Common Forms, the Biographical Sketch and the Current and Pending (Other) Support form, are produced, and NIH states that there is no blank template to complete outside it [1943](#cite:1943) [1942](#cite:1942) [249](#cite:249). Each agency adopts the forms on its own date: NSF already requires SciENcv for both documents, NIH requires it for due dates on or after January 25, 2026, DOE for funding opportunities published on or after January 1, 2026, and NASA accepts only its own NASA-specific SciENcv forms from September 1, 2026 [249](#cite:249) [248](#cite:248) [31](#cite:31) [1945](#cite:1945) [1946](#cite:1946). A person signs in with eRA Commons, ORCID, Login.gov, Google, Microsoft or academic institution credentials [1980](#cite:1980). A delegate may manage the documents, but the person named certifies the content [1980](#cite:1980) [257](#cite:257).

short: The interagency online system in which recipients of federal funding report inventions made under their awards to the funding agency.
definition: The interagency online system in which recipients of federal funding agreements report subject inventions to the funding agency and complete other reporting required under the Bayh-Dole Act [1951](#cite:1951). NIH built it in the 1990s and NIST has run it since around summer 2022 [1951](#cite:1951). The organisation registers at iedison.nist.gov, and each user holds an iEdison account and a Login.gov account under the same email address [1951](#cite:1951). The deadlines it serves are in the standard patent rights clause at 37 CFR 401.14: a subject invention is disclosed to the agency within two months after the inventor discloses it in writing, and the recipient elects whether to retain title within two years of disclosure [1952](#cite:1952). NIST lists agencies as they join, most recently MDA in September 2026 [1951](#cite:1951).

short: The site on which the next generation of Grants.gov is being built. Its search became the default search for federal funding opportunities in December 2025.
definition: The site on which HHS is building the next generation of Grants.gov [1967](#cite:1967). Its search became the default for searching for funding opportunities on December 23, 2025, and sign-in is through Login.gov [1920](#cite:1920) [1967](#cite:1967). Applying is mostly still done elsewhere: the home page says a user may need to visit Grants.gov to apply for most opportunities, and the roadmap lists two opportunities open for application through the site in late 2025 [1967](#cite:1967) [1919](#cite:1919). The roadmap gives three stages, the last of them 2027, when Simpler.Grants.gov replaces legacy Grants.gov and becomes the default experience; that stage is announced, with no day or month given [1919](#cite:1919).

short: The Internal Revenue Service's public look-up for tax-exempt organisations, where a funder checks a non-profit's standing and anyone can read its filed returns.
definition: The IRS's public look-up for exempt organisations [2059](#cite:2059). It searches the list of organisations eligible to receive tax-deductible contributions (Publication 78 data), Form 990 series returns, Form 990-N e-Postcards, determination letters and the Automatic Revocation of Exemption List [2059](#cite:2059). It is where a funder or donor checks a non-profit's standing, and it is one of the free sources that hold foundations' Form 990-PF filings [2059](#cite:2059). The IRS warns of delays in the tool's data, and the page carries the notice "We are still processing paper-filed 990 series received 2021 and later" [2059](#cite:2059).

short: The federal biomedical research agency, part of the Department of Health and Human Services. Its institutes and centers fund research at universities, medical schools and other organisations.
definition: The federal agency that describes itself as the largest public funder of biomedical research in the world; it is made up of 27 institutes and centers, each with its own research agenda [117](#cite:117) [143](#cite:143). Organisations that receive its grants can be domestic or foreign, public or private, non-profit or for-profit [117](#cite:117). From fiscal year 2026 Grants.gov is its single official source for grant and cooperative agreement funding opportunities [9](#cite:9). Review has two levels, a scientific review group and then the national advisory council or board of the institute that would pay, after which the institute or center director decides [38](#cite:38). Under the unified funding strategy, effective with the January 2026 council round, institutes do not rely on paylines [123](#cite:123) [13](#cite:13).

short: One of the component bodies of NIH, each with its own research agenda. The institute or center that would pay for an award decides whether to fund it.
definition: One of the component bodies of the National Institutes of Health, which says it is made up of 27 Institutes and Centers, each with a specific research agenda, often focusing on particular diseases or body systems [143](#cite:143). After peer review the advisory council makes funding recommendations to the institute or center director, who makes the funding decision [38](#cite:38). Each publishes the factors it weighs on its own funding-policy page, built on an NIH-wide framework that bars reliance on paylines from the January 2026 council round [67](#cite:67) [123](#cite:123). Some state rules that go beyond the NIH-wide ones, as NIAID does on multi-year funding [68](#cite:68). The FY 2027 budget request proposes to merge NIDA and NIAAA and to eliminate NCCIH, the Fogarty International Center and NIMHD; this is a request and has not been enacted [57](#cite:57).

short: The federal agency that funds research and education across science and engineering, through grants, cooperative agreements and fellowships.
definition: The federal agency that funds research and education across science and engineering through grants, cooperative agreements and fellowships [155](#cite:155). It is organised in eight directorates and posts its opportunities in its own Funding Search, on directorate pages and on Grants.gov [167](#cite:167) [155](#cite:155). Every proposal is judged on two criteria, Intellectual Merit and Broader Impacts; a programme officer obtains reviews from ad hoc reviewers, a panel or both, and then puts the proposal forward for award or decline [157](#cite:157) [160](#cite:160). NSF states that it receives approximately 43,000 proposals a year and makes roughly 8,300 awards [152](#cite:152). It has proposed to replace its Proposal and Award Policies and Procedures Guide with a Guidance on Financial Assistance; comments closed August 24, 2026, and NSF's stated goal is to issue it for use in early to mid FY2027 [152](#cite:152) [151](#cite:151).

short: One of the eight large units of the National Science Foundation. Each covers a group of fields, runs its own programmes and posts its own funding opportunities.
definition: One of the eight large units into which the National Science Foundation is organised: BIO, CISE, ENG, GEO, MPS, SBE, STEM Education (EDU) and TIP [167](#cite:167). Each covers a group of fields: BIO supports research and education on all forms of life, and MPS supports fundamental research in astronomical sciences, chemistry, materials, mathematical sciences and physics [182](#cite:182) [208](#cite:208) [209](#cite:209). A directorate posts opportunities on its own pages and in the NSF Funding Search, and its decisions follow NSF merit review [182](#cite:182) [155](#cite:155) [157](#cite:157). In December 2025 NSF realigned its divisions into sections, clusters or thematic areas to reduce layers [168](#cite:168) [177](#cite:177). The FY 2027 budget request states that NSF will close out SBE in FY 2027; this is a request and has not been enacted [255](#cite:255).

short: The part of the Department of Energy that funds basic research in the physical sciences and related fields at universities, non-profits, firms and national laboratories.
definition: The office of the Department of Energy that funds basic research in the physical sciences, computing, biology and environment, fusion, high energy physics, nuclear physics and isotopes, at universities, non-profits, firms and its national laboratories [277](#cite:277) [287](#cite:287). DOE describes it as the nation's largest supporter of basic research in the physical sciences and the steward of 10 national laboratories [367](#cite:367). Its annual open notice is posted at the end of September and stays open for the fiscal year, and targeted notices carry their own dates; both appear on its own site and on Grants.gov [277](#cite:277) [282](#cite:282) [364](#cite:364). The notice lists programme manager contacts by programme office and strongly encourages pre-applications [281](#cite:281). A programme manager screens each application and sends it to at least three reviewers, and a selection official decides, weighing the reviews, relevance to the mission, available funds and cost [286](#cite:286).

short: A defence research and development agency that funds universities and others. Its programme managers define programmes and choose who performs the work.
definition: A defence research funder that describes itself as an independent research and development agency within the U.S. Department of War, with six technical offices [343](#cite:343). It funds universities among others, through programme solicitations and office-wide announcements [345](#cite:345) [344](#cite:344). Programme managers define programmes and choose performers, and the office-wide announcements take ideas outside current programmes [343](#cite:343) [344](#cite:344). Each office keeps an office-wide announcement open for about a year or more, and programme solicitations appear as programmes start [347](#cite:347) [344](#cite:344). Notices are posted on SAM.gov and Grants.gov and linked from DARPA's site [344](#cite:344) [347](#cite:347).

short: A defence office that funds biomedical research in programmes named by Congress, with money Congress adds each year.
definition: A defence funder of biomedical research that began in 1992 with a congressional appropriation and works through programmes named by Congress [350](#cite:350). Its money is added by Congress each year and is not in the President's budget request [351](#cite:351). The totals move with the defense appropriation: $650 million for 12 programmes in FY 2025 and $1.27 billion for 34 programmes in FY 2026 [353](#cite:353) [295](#cite:295). Universities, medical schools, non-profits, firms and foreign organisations may apply as extramural organisations, and announcements appear on the CDMRP website, Grants.gov and eBRAP [330](#cite:330) [295](#cite:295). Review has two tiers, peer review for scientific merit and impact and then programmatic review for fit with the programme's vision and portfolio; consumer reviewers vote in both [352](#cite:352).

variants: Research Opportunities in Space and Earth Sciences
short: NASA's yearly omnibus call for research proposals in space and Earth science: one announcement holding many programme elements, each with its own scope and due dates.
definition: The omnibus research solicitation of NASA's Science Mission Directorate: one NASA Research Announcement holding many programme elements, each with its own scope and due dates [371](#cite:371) [372](#cite:372). Most of the directorate's research grants come through it [371](#cite:371). There is one a year, amended through the year; ROSES-2025 was released July 10, 2025, and NASA said in January 2026 that ROSES-2026 would be released in July 2026 [372](#cite:372) [294](#cite:294). Proposals go in through NSPIRES, and many elements use two steps, a Step-1 proposal or notice of intent and then the full proposal [377](#cite:377). Under ROSES-2025 dual-anonymous peer review is the default, and a selection official decides [375](#cite:375) [386](#cite:386).

term: National Institute of Food and Agriculture (NIFA)
short: The Department of Agriculture's agency for funding agricultural research, education and extension outside the department. AFRI is its largest competitive programme.
definition: The Department of Agriculture's extramural funding agency for agricultural research, education and extension [422](#cite:422). It has three kinds of funding: competitive grants; capacity grants to land-grant institutions, schools of forestry and schools of veterinary medicine; and non-competitive grants directed by Congress [422](#cite:422). Its Agriculture and Food Research Initiative (AFRI) is, in NIFA's words, "The nation's leading competitive grants program for agricultural sciences" [406](#cite:406). Notices are posted on NIFA's funding opportunities page and on Grants.gov, through which applications are submitted; peer review panels then rank the applications [408](#cite:408) [409](#cite:409) [422](#cite:422). USDA's FY 2027 Budget Summary proposes a cut of $510 million to NIFA formula grants, which is a request and has not been enacted [426](#cite:426).

short: The federal agency that funds the humanities, with grants to colleges, museums, libraries, research institutions, independent scholars and other non-profits.
definition: A federal grant-maker that describes itself as the largest federal funder of the humanities; it makes grants to colleges, universities, museums, libraries, historic sites, research institutions, independent scholars and other nonprofits [630](#cite:630). Since August 20, 2025 its grantmaking sits in four divisions [641](#cite:641). NEH posts each programme page and its Notice of Funding Opportunity on neh.gov and the application package on Grants.gov [630](#cite:630) [631](#cite:631) [646](#cite:646). Outside evaluators on peer review panels rate each application, NEH staff put applications forward in light of those ratings, the National Council on the Humanities reviews the staff's recommendations, and the Chair makes all final funding decisions [638](#cite:638). A district court on May 7, 2026 granted summary judgment against the April 2025 grant terminations, and a docket summary reports that the Government appealed to the Second Circuit on July 6, 2026 [642](#cite:642) [643](#cite:643).

short: The federal agency that funds arts projects by organisations, and research on the value and impact of the arts.
definition: A federal grant-maker for the arts: it funds arts projects by organisations and, through two research programmes, studies of the value and impact of the arts [650](#cite:650). Its Grants for Arts Projects programme gives standard applicants awards of $10,000 to $100,000 and requires a 1:1 cost share [654](#cite:654). It does not accept applications from individuals in these programmes, and an organisation without its own non-profit status may not use a fiscal sponsor or agent to submit an application [651](#cite:651) [654](#cite:654) [2065](#cite:2065). Guidelines are posted on arts.gov and the opportunity on Grants.gov; the second part of each application is filed in the NEA Applicant Portal [650](#cite:650) [652](#cite:652). Advisory panelists review applications in closed session, the National Council on the Arts votes on the panel's recommendations, and the Chair makes the final decision on all awards [652](#cite:652).

term: Institute of Museum and Library Services (IMLS)
short: The federal agency that makes grants to museums, libraries and related organisations.
definition: A federal grant-maker whose stated mission is advancing, supporting and empowering museums, libraries and related organisations through grantmaking, research and policy development [684](#cite:684). It posts each programme page and its Notice of Funding Opportunity on imls.gov and the opportunity on Grants.gov [676](#cite:676) [678](#cite:678) [679](#cite:679). IMLS screens for eligibility, peer reviewers who are professionals in the field score applications, and the Director makes the final funding decisions [677](#cite:677) [681](#cite:681). A district court on November 21, 2025 vacated the actions implementing Executive Order 14238 at IMLS and permanently enjoined further implementation [687](#cite:687). In a settlement dated April 9, 2026 IMLS agreed to continue awarding grants to the full extent of Congressional appropriation, using merit-based competitive peer review [689](#cite:689).

short: The statistics, research and evaluation arm of the Department of Education. Two of its centres run the department's education research grant competitions.
definition: The body that describes itself as the statistics, research, and evaluation arm of the U.S. Department of Education, established by the Education Sciences Reform Act of 2002, with four centres [669](#cite:669). Its research grant competitions are run by the National Center for Education Research and the National Center for Special Education Research [661](#cite:661). Requests for applications are posted on ies.ed.gov/funding, announced in the Federal Register, and applied to through Grants.gov [660](#cite:660) [662](#cite:662) [665](#cite:665). External experts review applications on panels, and programme officers, kept separate from the reviewers, make funding decisions using the scientific merit scores [666](#cite:666) [667](#cite:667). For FY 2027 IES is releasing its requests for applications in three tranches, the first on August 6, 2026 [661](#cite:661) [662](#cite:662).

term: Substance Abuse and Mental Health Services Administration (SAMHSA)
short: A Department of Health and Human Services agency that funds mental health and substance use services, training and capacity through block grants and discretionary grants.
definition: A federal agency that funds services, training and capacity through block and discretionary grants; its application guide says it expects most recipients will not fall under the human subjects regulations, and no research grant line was found [548](#cite:548) [549](#cite:549). Its two block grants go to the states, the District of Columbia, Puerto Rico, the U.S. Virgin Islands and Pacific jurisdictions, and a state agency applies for them [1129](#cite:1129) [1130](#cite:1130) [1219](#cite:1219). Discretionary applications go through eRA Commons ASSIST or Grants.gov Workspace and are evaluated by peer reviewers [548](#cite:548) [1113](#cite:1113). The programme office and approving official make the final determination, and National Advisory Council approval is required for awards over $250,000 [1112](#cite:1112). The FY2027 budget proposes to fold SAMHSA into an Administration for a Healthy America, which the budget documents describe as planned [533](#cite:533) [535](#cite:535).

short: A Department of Health and Human Services agency that is mainly a funder of health services and the health workforce, with a small research line in maternal and child health.
definition: A federal agency that is mainly a service and workforce funder; its research grant line sits in the Maternal and Child Health Bureau's Office of Epidemiology and Research [569](#cite:569) [568](#cite:568). Its find-funding page displays all open and closed opportunities [1145](#cite:1145). Each notice sets who can apply, and an application that is ineligible, incomplete, non-responsive or late is not reviewed [1215](#cite:1215) [1147](#cite:1147). A panel of independent experts scores the rest against the criteria in the notice, HRSA decides, and the Notice of Award states the budget period, amount, terms and reports [1147](#cite:1147). The FY2027 budget proposes to fold HRSA into an Administration for a Healthy America, which the justification describes as planned [535](#cite:535) [533](#cite:533).

short: The Department of Health and Human Services agency for children, youth and family programmes, among them Head Start and block grants to states and tribes.
definition: The HHS agency for children, youth and family programmes: it runs Head Start, the Runaway and Homeless Youth grants and other programmes as direct competitions, and the Community Services Block Grant, Social Services Block Grant and child care funds as formula money to states and tribes [1339](#cite:1339) [1234](#cite:1234) [1239](#cite:1239) [1241](#cite:1241) [1248](#cite:1248). Its notices, forecasts and archived notices are on Grants.gov [1224](#cite:1224). Competitive applications are scored by review panels whose members are typically not federal employees, against criteria and point values printed in each notice [1235](#cite:1235) [1246](#cite:1246). For Head Start, ACF states that review scores and rankings do not bind it [1228](#cite:1228). HHS announced on March 27, 2025 that ACL's programmes would be integrated into ACF, ASPE and CMS, and the FY2027 budget presents ACF and ACL together as the Administration for Children, Families, and Communities and calls the integration planned [530](#cite:530) [1339](#cite:1339).

short: The Department of Health and Human Services agency that funds services for older adults and people with disabilities. NIDILRR is its disability research institute.
definition: A federal agency that funds services for older adults and people with disabilities; most of its money is formula funding under the Older Americans Act that passes through state and area agencies on aging, and it also makes direct discretionary grants [1260](#cite:1260) [1259](#cite:1259) [1255](#cite:1255). Its research institute, the National Institute on Disability, Independent Living, and Rehabilitation Research (NIDILRR), funds disability and rehabilitation research under Title II of the Rehabilitation Act [576](#cite:576) [582](#cite:582) [581](#cite:581). ACL posts on Grants.gov and on its own open-opportunities page, which sorts by programme office [1259](#cite:1259) [1044](#cite:1044). For NIDILRR an independent panel of at least three reviewers scores each application and the ACL Administrator makes final decisions [579](#cite:579) [578](#cite:578). HHS announced on March 27, 2025 that ACL's programmes would be integrated into ACF, ASPE and CMS; the FY2027 justification describes the integration as planned, and ACL was still posting notices under its own name in 2026 [530](#cite:530) [1339](#cite:1339) [1255](#cite:1255).

term: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC)
short: A Department of Health and Human Services agency that funds outside research through its centres and institutes, among them NIOSH, its institute for occupational safety and health.
definition: A federal agency that funds extramural research through its centres and institutes, among them the National Institute for Occupational Safety and Health (NIOSH), which uses NIH-style activity codes, and the Injury Center [552](#cite:552) [556](#cite:556) [551](#cite:551) [560](#cite:560). All CDC grant and cooperative agreement opportunities are posted on Grants.gov [550](#cite:550). At NIOSH, scientists from outside the agency carry out initial review in a study section or special emphasis panels, and the NIOSH Secondary Review Committee then reviews for programme relevance and portfolio balance [552](#cite:552). NIOSH's standing R01 announcement expired on November 21, 2025 [556](#cite:556). A district court on July 1, 2025 enjoined further reductions in force and restructuring under the March 27, 2025 announcement at CDC and three other HHS components, and the First Circuit denied a stay on September 17, 2025 [542](#cite:542) [543](#cite:543).

term: Agency for Healthcare Research and Quality (AHRQ)
short: The Department of Health and Human Services agency for health services research: the quality, safety and delivery of health care.
definition: The HHS agency for health services research; the priorities its funding page names are healthcare quality and safety, delivery and practice improvement, and whole-person care [504](#cite:504). Its announcements are posted in the NIH Guide for Grants and Contracts, with an index on ahrq.gov [518](#cite:518) [519](#cite:519). Applications were assigned to a peer review group or special emphasis panel, and funding decisions were described as based on merit, priorities and available funds [506](#cite:506) [520](#cite:520) [507](#cite:507). Between March 6 and March 17, 2026 AHRQ issued early expiration notices for its R01, R03, R18, R36 and topic-specific announcements [512](#cite:512) [513](#cite:513) [514](#cite:514) [515](#cite:515) [516](#cite:516) [517](#cite:517). HHS announced in March 2025 that AHRQ would merge with ASPE into an Office of Strategy, and the FY2027 budget places AHRQ in that office [530](#cite:530) [536](#cite:536).

short: An independent non-profit research funder, authorised by Congress, that pays for studies comparing how well clinical options work for patients. Its awards are contracts.
definition: An independent non-profit funder of patient-centered comparative clinical effectiveness research, which Congress authorized in 2010 and reauthorized in December 2019 [586](#cite:586). It is paid for by the Patient-Centered Outcomes Research Trust Fund, which receives appropriations and a fee on private insurance and self-insured health plans for fiscal years 2020 through 2029; PCORI receives 80 percent of the Trust Fund [587](#cite:587). Its awards are contracts, and a letter of intent is required before an application [599](#cite:599). It posts on its own funding opportunities page and runs three research cycles a year [590](#cite:590). Invited full applications go to merit review panels of scientific, patient and other stakeholder reviewers whose scores are weighted equally [597](#cite:597).

short: The federal national service agency. It funds organisations to engage members and volunteers in service.
definition: The federal agency, formally the Corporation for National and Community Service, that funds organisations to engage members and volunteers in service through State and National grants, VISTA and the AmeriCorps Seniors programmes [1374](#cite:1374) [1379](#cite:1379) [1378](#cite:1378).
