State and National money is split by regulation between a population formula to States, a competition among States and direct competitive grants [1377](#cite:1377). Notices are posted on Grants.gov, with the full notice and resources on the competition page at americorps.gov [1374](#cite:1374). In April 2025 the agency terminated 1,031 grants; a preliminary injunction of June 5, 2025 bars the closure of the terminated programmes in 24 plaintiff States and the District of Columbia, pending notice-and-comment rulemaking [1380](#cite:1380).

short: An independent non-profit set up by Congress that passes its annual appropriation to local non-profit legal aid programmes.
definition: An independent 501(c)(3) non-profit established by Congress in 1974 and funded by annual appropriation, governed by a board of 11 members appointed by the President and confirmed by the Senate [1328](#cite:1328). It distributes over 94 percent of its funding to 129 independent non-profit legal aid programmes [1328](#cite:1328). For Basic Field Grants the request for proposals comes in April, applications are due June 1, and decisions are announced in December for the following calendar year [1325](#cite:1325) [1324](#cite:1324). It posts on lsc.gov and takes applications in its own system, GrantEase [1324](#cite:1324). Congress passed $540 million for FY2026 after the White House proposed in May 2025 to eliminate LSC and the House Appropriations Committee approved $300 million [1329](#cite:1329) [1330](#cite:1330).

short: HUD's yearly homeless assistance competition, and the local body through which projects enter it. A project goes into that body's single application and does not apply alone.
definition: The Department of Housing and Urban Development programme that funds non-profit providers, states, tribes and local governments to rehouse people who are homeless and to run the housing and services that go with it, under 24 CFR part 578 [1347](#cite:1347). The name also covers the local body for an area: a project applicant does not apply alone, and its project goes into the consolidated application that the local Continuum of Care's Collaborative Applicant submits in e-snaps [1286](#cite:1286) [1283](#cite:1283). The local CoC ranks its projects and HUD then selects in two tiers [1286](#cite:1286). Recipients match all grant funds except leasing funds with no less than 25 percent in cash or in-kind contributions [1286](#cite:1286). The FY2026 notice was vacated by a district court, restored by an appeals-court stay and closed on September 30, 2026, and HUD's FY2027 budget requests no funding for the programme [1283](#cite:1283) [1340](#cite:1340).

short: The Department of Justice's main grant-making office. Its bureaus fund reentry, victim services, juvenile justice and related programmes.
definition: The Department of Justice's main grant-making office; three of its bureaus fund services: BJA (reentry, treatment courts, justice assistance), OVC (victim services and the Victims of Crime Act formula grants) and OJJDP (mentoring, youth reentry, juvenile justice formula grants) [612](#cite:612) [1280](#cite:1280) [1344](#cite:1344). Notices are posted on the OJP Current Funding Opportunities page and on Grants.gov, and applications are completed in JustGrants [612](#cite:612) [619](#cite:619). Applications are screened for basic minimum requirements, then go through merit-based review and programmatic and financial review; final decisions are made by the Assistant Attorney General unless a statute names another official [619](#cite:619). In April 2025 OJP terminated 376 discretionary awards to 219 recipients, citing 2 C.F.R. 200.340(a)(4); on July 7, 2025 a district court dismissed the challenge for lack of jurisdiction, and an appeal was argued October 14, 2025 [1281](#cite:1281) [1282](#cite:1282).

term: Department of Health and Human Services (HHS)
short: The federal department that holds NIH, CDC, HRSA, SAMHSA, ACF, ACL and AHRQ. Its grants policy statement covers its agencies other than NIH.
definition: The federal department whose grant-making agencies include ACF, ACL, AHRQ, CDC, FDA, HRSA, IHS and SAMHSA; these follow the HHS Grants Policy Statement, which does not apply to awards made by NIH [527](#cite:527). Version 2.0 of that statement took effect October 1, 2025, and on the same date HHS adopted 2 CFR 200 with modifications at 2 CFR 300 [527](#cite:527) [528](#cite:528). On March 27, 2025 HHS announced a reorganisation: 28 divisions consolidated into 15, a new Administration for a Healthy America combining OASH, HRSA, SAMHSA, ATSDR and NIOSH, and AHRQ merged with ASPE into an Office of Strategy [530](#cite:530). The FY 2027 budget documents describe the Administration for a Healthy America as planned; FY 2026 appropriations were reported under SAMHSA and HRSA as separate agencies [535](#cite:535) [533](#cite:533).

short: A college or university, as a class of applicant in federal grant notices. Notices list it apart from other non-profits, and some programmes are open to it alone.
definition: A college or university, treated in federal notices as its own class of applicant: both non-profit categories on Grants.gov are worded as "other than institutions of higher education" [2064](#cite:2064). The test differs by funder: NSF counts two- and four-year institutions, community colleges included, accredited in and with a campus located in the U.S., while a Department of Transportation notice uses the definition at 20 U.S.C. 1001(a) [156](#cite:156) [493](#cite:493). The Uniform Guidance names institutions of higher education among the non-federal entities it covers [1894](#cite:1894) [1845](#cite:1845). Some programmes are limited to them, the NIH R15 among them [7](#cite:7).

short: A non-profit that the IRS has recognised as tax-exempt under section 501(c)(3). Federal notices and many foundations ask for this status by name.
definition: A non-profit that the Internal Revenue Service has recognised as tax-exempt, normally on an application on Form 1023 or Form 1023-EZ; federal notices describe the standing as "nonprofits having a 501(c)(3) status with the IRS" [2064](#cite:2064) [2046](#cite:2046). State law governs non-profit status and federal law governs tax-exempt status, so an organisation can be a non-profit under state law without this recognition [2047](#cite:2047). A funder checks the status in the IRS Tax Exempt Organization Search, which holds determination letters, filed returns and the Automatic Revocation List [2059](#cite:2059). The status is lost automatically after three consecutive years without an annual return or notice [2057](#cite:2057). Every organisation with the status is classified as either a private foundation or a public charity [2054](#cite:2054).

short: A 501(c)(3) organisation that the IRS has not classed as a private foundation, such as a school, a hospital, a church or a body supported by the public.
definition: One of the two classes into which every section 501(c)(3) organisation falls; the other is the private foundation [2054](#cite:2054). An organisation is presumed to be a private foundation unless it requests and qualifies for a determination as a public charity [2054](#cite:2054). The class includes churches, schools, hospitals, medical research organisations, publicly supported organisations that receive a specified portion of their support from public sources, and certain supporting organisations [2054](#cite:2054). The difference shows in the annual return and the rules: a private foundation files Form 990-PF whatever its size and is subject to operating restrictions and excise taxes [2055](#cite:2055) [2054](#cite:2054). Some funders ask for this class by name; one community trust limits grants to section 501(c)(3) agencies "that are not classified as private foundations" [2423](#cite:2423).

short: An arrangement in which one organisation oversees the money side for a project or group that has no tax-exempt status of its own. Funders differ on whether they accept it.
definition: An arrangement in which one body handles the finances of another: a fiscal sponsor, in the Arts Endowment's words, is an entity that oversees the fiscal activities of another organisation, company, or group of independent artists or projects [2065](#cite:2065). A newcomer might assume it opens federal grants to a group without its own status, but the two federal pages read for this guide do not accept an application made that way [2065](#cite:2065) [648](#cite:648). At the Arts Endowment an organisation without its own non-profit status may not use a fiscal sponsor or agent to submit an application, and an NEH notice of March 12, 2026 says fiscal sponsors applying on behalf of an ineligible organisation are not eligible [2065](#cite:2065) [648](#cite:648). Foundations differ: Open Society Foundations lets informal groups come through a fiscal sponsor or intermediary, and the Simons Foundation does not fund fiscal sponsors or agents [2357](#cite:2357) [2120](#cite:2120).

variants: Established Program to Stimulate Competitive Research
short: A programme at NSF, with counterparts at other agencies, to raise the research competitiveness of listed states and territories. An institution qualifies by where it is.
definition: NSF's programme, in full the Established Program to Stimulate Competitive Research, to raise the research competitiveness of targeted jurisdictions, each a state, territory or commonwealth [866](#cite:866). NSF lists 28 eligible jurisdictions, and its eligibility page says the CHIPS and Science Act of 2022 in effect freezes jurisdiction eligibility through FY 2027 [878](#cite:878) [877](#cite:877). An institution's location in an eligible jurisdiction decides whether it can apply to the EPSCoR Graduate Fellowship Program and EPSCoR Research Fellows, and EPSCoR often co-funds proposals sent to other NSF programmes without a separate application [825](#cite:825) [867](#cite:867) [1518](#cite:1518). Other agencies keep lists for their own capacity programmes and the lists are not the same: DOE and NASA follow the NSF list, DEPSCoR lists 36 states and territories, and USDA lists 19 states for FY 2026 plus the District of Columbia and insular areas [1567](#cite:1567) [1574](#cite:1574) [1565](#cite:1565) [1576](#cite:1576).

short: NIH's programme to build biomedical research capacity in states that have had low levels of NIH funding. An institution qualifies by being in a listed state.
definition: A congressionally mandated NIH programme that builds research capacity in states that historically have had low levels of NIH funding; the Division for Research Capacity Building at the National Institute of General Medical Sciences administers it [1543](#cite:1543). An institution is eligible by its location, and the list is 23 states and Puerto Rico [1546](#cite:1546) [1584](#cite:1584). The programme has five components: COBRE, INBRE, the clinical and translational research programmes, co-funding, and the regional entrepreneurship programme I-RED [1543](#cite:1543). Under co-funding NIGMS adds up to $350,000 in total costs for each of the first two years to R01, R15 and MIRA R35 applications from investigators in IDeA states that an NIH institute did not select for funding [1553](#cite:1553). The pages and notices read do not state the rule by which a state enters or leaves the list, which is not the same as the NSF EPSCoR list [1543](#cite:1543) [1545](#cite:1545) [1517](#cite:1517).

short: A college or university placed in a class defined by the students it enrols or by its history. Funders define the class in different ways, so the notice in hand decides.
definition: A college or university that a funder places in a class defined by the students it enrols or by its history; the definitions differ from one funder to the next [423](#cite:423) [579](#cite:579). NIFA counts an institution where one or more minority groups exceed 50 percent of enrolment [423](#cite:423). A NIDILRR notice counts a historically black college or university, a Hispanic-serving institution, an American Indian tribal college or university, or another institution where minority student enrollment is at least 50 percent [579](#cite:579). NASA checks eligibility against its own NASA MSI List, while the Department of Education's FY 2025 Eligibility Matrix holds programme lists for the minority-serving classes, HBCUs and TCCUs [1629](#cite:1629) [1595](#cite:1595). On December 2, 2025 the Office of Legal Counsel concluded that the Department of Education's three HSI programmes and its AANAPISI programme are unconstitutional and inseverable [1592](#cite:1592).

short: A college or university founded before 1964 with the principal mission of educating Black Americans. The class is closed: statute and a list in regulation fix it.
definition: An institution established before 1964 whose principal mission was the education of Black Americans, authorised by its state and accredited or preaccredited [1602](#cite:1602). The class is closed: it is fixed by statute and by a list in the Department of Education's regulation at 34 CFR 608.2, not by current enrolment [1649](#cite:1649). Executive Order 14283 defines the term by reference to that list, and the Defense and NIH notices read for this guide use the same statutory definition [1618](#cite:1618) [1627](#cite:1627) [1656](#cite:1656). That order, signed April 23, 2025, set up a White House Initiative on HBCUs and directs agencies to file annual plans [1618](#cite:1618). The Office of Legal Counsel opinion of December 2, 2025 on Department of Education programmes says it does not opine on HBCU programmes [1592](#cite:1592).

short: A college that meets the Title V tests for an eligible institution and whose full-time-equivalent undergraduate enrolment is at least 25 percent Hispanic. The status follows enrolment.
definition: An eligible institution under Title V whose undergraduate full-time-equivalent enrolment is at least 25 percent Hispanic at the end of the award year before it applies [1647](#cite:1647). The status follows enrolment and is shown when an institution applies; it is not a permanent list [1642](#cite:1642). In the Department of Education's last competition the applicant documented the 25 percent and the Department checked it against IPEDS and other data [1642](#cite:1642). The definition is in litigation: the Justice Department told Congress on July 25, 2025 that it would not defend it in State of Tennessee v. U.S. Department of Education, and on December 2, 2025 the Office of Legal Counsel concluded that the Department's three HSI programmes are unconstitutional and inseverable [1606](#cite:1606) [1592](#cite:1592). A law firm summary of September 30, 2026 reports that the court had not ruled on the intervenor's motions [1650](#cite:1650).

short: A college that qualifies under one of the federal statutes on tribally controlled colleges, or is named among the 1994 land-grant institutions. Statute sets the class.
definition: An institution that qualifies under the Tribally Controlled College or University Assistance Act of 1978 or the Navajo Community College Assistance Act of 1978, or is named in section 532 of the Equity in Educational Land-Grant Status Act of 1994 [1617](#cite:1617). Section 532 names 36 colleges in the 2023 edition of the United States Code, and the Act treats them as land-grant colleges [1641](#cite:1641). For the Department of Education programme a new applicant needs an eligibility determination from the Bureau of Indian Education, and existing grantees no longer apply for eligibility [1617](#cite:1617). NSF uses the section 532 list and the 1978 Act for its Tribal Colleges and Universities Program [1613](#cite:1613). On August 12, 2026 the Office of Legal Counsel concluded that NSF awards to tribal colleges fall within the Morton v. Mancari exception and are constitutional [876](#cite:876).

short: A college that awards associate's, bachelor's or master's degrees and few doctorates. NSF uses the class for its RUI and ROA opportunities.
definition: An accredited college or university, two-year community colleges included, that awards associate's, bachelor's or master's degrees in NSF-supported fields and few doctorates [254](#cite:254). NSF's test is a count: the institution has awarded 20 or fewer Ph.D./D.Sci. degrees in all NSF-supported fields during the combined previous two academic years [254](#cite:254). The institution certifies its own standing, and an RUI proposal carries a Certification of RUI/ROA Eligibility [254](#cite:254). NIH's R15 AREA programme uses a different test of undergraduate focus: undergraduate enrolment greater than graduate enrolment, and limited NIH support [7](#cite:7).

short: A college or university that holds land-grant status under federal laws of 1862, 1890 or 1994. The status opens NIFA capacity funding and programmes reserved for each group.
definition: A college or university in one of three groups that NIFA's directory names: the 1862 public universities, the 1890 historically Black universities and the 1994 tribal colleges [1636](#cite:1636). Statute defines land-grant colleges and universities as institutions eligible for funds under the Act of July 2, 1862 or the Act of August 30, 1890 [1640](#cite:1640). NIFA lists 19 universities in the 1890 group, and section 532 of the Equity in Educational Land-Grant Status Act of 1994 names the 1994 Institutions, which the Act treats as land-grant colleges [1637](#cite:1637) [1641](#cite:1641). NIFA's capacity grants go to land-grant institutions, schools of forestry and schools of veterinary medicine [422](#cite:422).

short: A university that the Carnegie Classification places among Doctoral Universities with Very High Research Activity. Some programmes are open only to institutions outside that group.
definition: A university that the Carnegie Classification places among Doctoral Universities with Very High Research Activity [832](#cite:832) [828](#cite:828). A newcomer might expect the label to open doors, but in the notices read for this guide it works the other way: several NSF career-stage and training programmes are open only to institutions not currently classified R1, among them Engineering Research Initiation and Track 2 of the Research Traineeship [832](#cite:832) [828](#cite:828). The Department of Energy's Visiting Faculty Program excludes institutions classed Research 1 or Research 2 in the 2025 Carnegie Classification, though faculty at Historically Black Colleges and Universities qualify whatever the classification [902](#cite:902). Eligibility is read from the institution's Carnegie Classification, as each solicitation states [832](#cite:832) [828](#cite:828).

term: Title III and Title V eligibility
short: A yearly Department of Education designation of colleges that enrol many needy students and spend little per student. Certain Higher Education Act grant programmes require it.
definition: A designation the Department of Education makes each year under section 312 of the Higher Education Act: an "eligible institution" is a college that enrols a high share of needy students and has low core expenses per student compared with institutions of its type [1596](#cite:1596) [1595](#cite:1595). A designated institution may apply for the grant programmes that require it and may receive a one-year waiver of certain non-Federal cost-sharing requirements [1595](#cite:1595). The Department pre-determines eligibility from IPEDS data in the Eligibility Matrix; an institution checks its status in the Grant Eligibility Application system at HEPIS.ed.gov and, if not shown as eligible, applies for reconsideration or a waiver within the yearly window [1596](#cite:1596). The FY 2026 notice is titled for programmes under section 312 only, where the FY 2025 notice was titled for Parts A and F of Title III and Title V [1596](#cite:1596) [1597](#cite:1597).

short: A lender certified by the Treasury's CDFI Fund to lend and invest in its community. Certification is the gate to the Fund's Financial Assistance awards.
definition: A lender that the Community Development Financial Institutions Fund has certified; the Fund's Financial Assistance awards go to certified institutions to lend and invest in their communities [1433](#cite:1433). Certification is the gate to those awards: each Financial Assistance applicant must be a certified CDFI [1434](#cite:1434). An Emerging CDFI, an organisation not yet certified that shows an acceptable plan to meet the certification requirements by the end of its period of performance, may apply for Technical Assistance [1434](#cite:1434) [1433](#cite:1433). A non-profit lender may apply once it holds or is working toward certification; a non-profit that does not lend is not eligible [1434](#cite:1434). Certification is decided by the CDFI Fund on application, and the application's information collection was put out for comment on September 30, 2026 [1436](#cite:1436).

short: A tax-exempt charity that falls outside the tax code's categories of public charity. It files a public return, Form 990-PF, every year.
definition: The class into which the tax code puts every section 501(c)(3) organisation that does not fall into an excluded category; the excluded organisations are the public charities [2237](#cite:2237) [2238](#cite:2238). It files Form 990-PF each year whatever its size and is subject to excise taxes and operating restrictions that a public charity is not [2055](#cite:2055) [2054](#cite:2054). The grantmaking kind, the non-operating foundation, must also pay out a minimum amount each year [2375](#cite:2375) [2377](#cite:2377). The return is public and lists every grant paid, so a reader can see what the foundation has funded [2387](#cite:2387) [2461](#cite:2461). The word in an organisation's name does not settle the class: a community foundation that meets a public support test is a public charity [2374](#cite:2374).

short: A kind label on this guide's funder records for a private foundation that is not a company's, a community's or an operating foundation.
definition: A label of this guide's own on 39 of its 65 foundation and private grantmaker records. It is shorthand for a private foundation that the record does not mark as a family, corporate, community or operating foundation, and the pages read for the guide give no legal definition of the word. In law each such body is a private foundation: every section 501(c)(3) organisation is one unless it falls into an excluded category, and all private foundations file Form 990-PF each year [2237](#cite:2237).

short: A kind label on four of this guide's funder records. In law a family foundation is a private foundation like any other.
definition: A label of this guide's own on four of its funder records: the Gordon and Betty Moore Foundation, The David and Lucile Packard Foundation, Bloomberg Philanthropies and the Walton Family Foundation. The pages read for the guide give no legal definition of the term, and the label follows how each is commonly described. In law each is a private foundation unless it falls into an excluded category, and all private foundations file Form 990-PF each year [2237](#cite:2237).

short: A grantmaking public charity that serves one local area. Part of what it pays out follows the advice of its donors and is not open to application.
definition: A charity that attracts large contributions for the benefit of a particular community or area and makes grants there; the IRS's term is community trust [2374](#cite:2374) [2405](#cite:2405). One that meets a public support test is a public charity, not a private foundation, and files Form 990 with Schedule A, so it has no Form 990-PF line on unsolicited requests [2374](#cite:2374). The Council on Foundations counts more than 900 of them [2405](#cite:2405). A community foundation pays out money in two ways, and only one takes applications: competitive grants decided by its staff and board, and donor-advised grants that follow the advice of the donor who set up the fund [2416](#cite:2416) [2428](#cite:2428) [2373](#cite:2373). Its own website is the place to learn how it takes applications [2374](#cite:2374) [2432](#cite:2432).

short: A private foundation whose assets come mainly from a for-profit company. A corporate giving programme is a different thing: it is run inside the company and files no public return of its own.
definition: A private foundation whose assets come mainly from the contributions of a for-profit business, which Candid's glossary calls a company-sponsored foundation; a company can also give through a corporate giving programme, set up and run inside the company itself [2408](#cite:2408). The first is a separate legal body that files Form 990-PF, and the second files no public return of its own [2408](#cite:2408) [2387](#cite:2387). The IRS pages read for this guide do not define a corporate foundation as a class of its own; as a private foundation it falls under the general rule [2237](#cite:2237). The corporate funders read pair an open route for small local grants, or a fixed annual window, with national grants by invitation [2433](#cite:2433) [2441](#cite:2441) [2438](#cite:2438). From tax years beginning after December 31, 2025 a corporation may deduct charitable gifts only above 1 percent of taxable income [2392](#cite:2392) [2395](#cite:2395).

short: A private foundation that devotes most of its resources to carrying out its own charitable activities. The tax on failing to pay out a minimum amount does not apply to it.
definition: A private foundation that devotes most of its resources to the active conduct of its own exempt activities [2371](#cite:2371). It is not subject to the excise tax on failure to distribute income, and it still pays the tax on net investment income and follows the other private foundation rules [2371](#cite:2371). A foundation claiming the status completes Part XIII of Form 990-PF, and any grants it paid still appear in Part XIV, line 3 [2388](#cite:2388) [2387](#cite:2387). The other kind, the non-operating foundation, filed 91.2% of private foundation returns for tax year 2022 [2410](#cite:2410). The short application for tax exemption, Form 1023-EZ, is closed to private operating foundations [2050](#cite:2050).

short: A separately identified fund held by a sponsoring charity. The sponsor has legal control of the money, and the donor keeps the right to advise where grants go.
definition: A separately identified fund or account that a section 501(c)(3) organisation, called a sponsoring organisation, maintains and operates [2373](#cite:2373). Once the donor gives, the sponsoring organisation has legal control of the money, and the donor or the donor's representative keeps advisory privileges over distributions and investments [2373](#cite:2373). Community foundations are among the sponsors, and a grant from such a fund starts with the donor's advice, not with an application to the sponsor [2428](#cite:2428) [2373](#cite:2373). The New York Community Trust tells applicants "We cannot refer you to donors" [2416](#cite:2416). Gifts to donor-advised funds do not qualify for the deduction for non-itemisers that begins with tax year 2026 [2389](#cite:2389).

short: A charity that counts as a public charity because of its relationship to one or more other public charities that it supports.
definition: A charity that is a public charity because of its relationship to one or more other public charities that it supports [2238](#cite:2238). It must satisfy an organizational test, an operational test, a control test and a relationship test, and comes in three types [2372](#cite:2372). Type I is operated, supervised or controlled by its supported organisation, Type II is supervised or controlled in connection with it, and Type III is either functionally integrated or not [2372](#cite:2372). A Type III organisation that is not functionally integrated has its own payout rule: the greater of 85 percent of adjusted net income and 3.5 percent of the value of its non-exempt-use assets [2372](#cite:2372). Supporting organisations cannot use the short application, Form 1023-EZ [2050](#cite:2050).

short: A public charity whose main purpose is medical research and which carries that research out itself, in conjunction with a hospital.
definition: A public charity whose principal purpose or function is to engage in medical research and that is directly engaged in the continuous active conduct of medical research in conjunction with a hospital [2374](#cite:2374). The IRS lists qualified medical research organisations affiliated with hospitals among the public charities [2238](#cite:2238). Under 26 CFR 1.170A-9(d)(2) one meets the test if it devotes more than one half of its assets to that research or spends 3.5 percent or more of the fair market value of its endowment on it [2239](#cite:2239). It states its status on Schedule A of Form 990 and does not file Form 990-PF [2374](#cite:2374) [2238](#cite:2238). The Howard Hughes Medical Institute files Form 990 and calls itself "a medical research organization"; its Investigators are its employees and receive no grant [2164](#cite:2164) [2160](#cite:2160) [2161](#cite:2161).

short: The annual return every private foundation files with the IRS. It is public and shows the foundation's assets, every grant paid, and whether it takes unsolicited requests.
definition: The annual return that every private foundation files with the IRS, whatever its size; a 2025 return must be filed electronically [2388](#cite:2388) [2055](#cite:2055). It is public: a foundation must make it available for inspection and copying for three years [2461](#cite:2461). Four places answer most of a grant seeker's questions: the asset figure on page 1, the grants paid line in Part I, the balance sheet in Part II, and Part XIV, which lists every grant and says whether the foundation takes requests [2387](#cite:2387). A foundation that checks the box on Part XIV, line 2 is saying that it gives only to charities it has chosen itself [2387](#cite:2387). A community foundation or other public charity files Form 990 with Schedule A instead [2374](#cite:2374).

short: The annual return a tax-exempt organisation files with the IRS. Small organisations file the shorter Form 990-EZ or the electronic notice Form 990-N.
definition: The annual return that a tax-exempt organisation files with the IRS; which form in the series it files depends on its size and on whether it is a private foundation [2055](#cite:2055). Form 990-N, the e-Postcard, is for gross receipts normally of $50,000 or less; Form 990-EZ may be used with gross receipts under $200,000 and total assets under $500,000; at or above either of those two figures the organisation files Form 990 [2055](#cite:2055). Churches are excepted from filing, and an organisation that files nothing for three consecutive years loses its tax-exempt status automatically [2056](#cite:2056) [2057](#cite:2057). Returns are open to public inspection for three years, and the IRS Tax Exempt Organization Search holds filed returns [2461](#cite:2461) [2059](#cite:2059). On Schedule A a public charity states the reason it is not a private foundation [2374](#cite:2374).

short: An identifying number the IRS issues to an organisation. A new organisation obtains one before it applies for tax exemption, and its filings are looked up by it.
definition: An identifying number that the IRS issues to an organisation; obtaining one is among the things the IRS says an organisation does before it applies for tax-exempt status [2047](#cite:2047) [2089](#cite:2089). The online application is free, an approved number is issued immediately, and a corporation is formed with the state before applying [2089](#cite:2089). Agencies ask for it: the agency that starts an ASAP.gov payment enrolment uses the recipient's UEI and EIN, and a request for an IRS affirmation letter gives the organisation's name and EIN [1956](#cite:1956) [2066](#cite:2066). ProPublica's Nonprofit Explorer, a database of non-profit tax filings, gives each organisation a page reached by its EIN [2398](#cite:2398) [2415](#cite:2415).

short: The amount a grantmaking private foundation must pay out for charitable purposes each year, worked out from 5 percent of its investment assets.
definition: The least that a private non-operating foundation must pay out for charitable purposes each year [2375](#cite:2375). The sum starts from the minimum investment return, which is 5 percent of the excess of the value of the foundation's assets not used for its exempt purposes over the debt incurred to buy them, and the distributable amount is that return reduced by income taxes and the tax on investment income [2377](#cite:2377) [2376](#cite:2376). A foundation that fails to pay it out in time owes a 30 percent excise tax on the undistributed income under section 4942, and a further 100 percent if the shortfall is not made up within 90 days of IRS notification [2375](#cite:2375). Private operating foundations are not subject to this tax [2371](#cite:2371). The median payout rate for tax year 2022 was 5.71%, and MacArthur set its own baseline at 6 percent through 2028 [2410](#cite:2410) [2326](#cite:2326) [2328](#cite:2328).

short: A short first request to a foundation. The foundation reads it and then invites a full proposal from some of those who sent one.
definition: A brief letter outlining an organisation's activities and its request for funding, sent to a foundation as the first of two steps [2408](#cite:2408) [2216](#cite:2216). The foundation reads it and invites a full proposal from some applicants; a full proposal sent without an invitation is not read [2124](#cite:2124) [2216](#cite:2216). Foundations use other names for the same step, among them letter of intent, concept note and online funding inquiry, and each sets its own form, length, deadline and reply time [2121](#cite:2121) [2219](#cite:2219) [2155](#cite:2155) [2201](#cite:2201). Sloan takes one by email and says a reply can take up to 8 weeks, and Kellogg decides within 30 business days [2124](#cite:2124) [2269](#cite:2269). Some foundations take none: Mott has not accepted unsolicited letters of inquiry or proposals since January 2025 [2298](#cite:2298).

short: A foundation's rule that it takes proposals only from organisations it has itself approached. A proposal sent without an invitation is not accepted.
definition: A way of making grants in which a foundation's staff find organisations themselves and invite a proposal, and a proposal from an organisation the foundation has not approached is not accepted [2300](#cite:2300) [2304](#cite:2304). Each foundation states the rule in its own words: Ford's are "We do not accept any unsolicited grant proposals by mail, email or phone.", and Walmart adds that "invitations are not granted upon request" [2259](#cite:2259) [2433](#cite:2433). Of the 25 large national foundations in this guide's records, 17 are marked invitation-only [2259](#cite:2259) [2298](#cite:2298) [2307](#cite:2307). Such foundations say that an invitation follows from staff coming to know an organisation's work, and a few name a first contact an outsider may make, as Kresge does with its contact form [2307](#cite:2307) [2348](#cite:2348). Some also post open calls [2274](#cite:2274) [2349](#cite:2349).

short: A dated competition that a foundation opens to organisations it has not approached, with its own page, deadline and eligibility rule.
definition: A route that an invitation-only foundation opens to organisations it has not approached; request for proposals (RFP) is another name for it [2274](#cite:2274) [2349](#cite:2349). Each call has its own page, dates and eligibility rule, and any organisation that meets the call's own rule may apply [2321](#cite:2321) [2355](#cite:2355). Foundations post calls on a dedicated page, such as Kresge's current funding opportunities and Wallace's requests for proposals, and Hewlett issues open calls occasionally [2274](#cite:2274) [2349](#cite:2349) [2280](#cite:2280). A foundation may have none posted: neither of those two pages listed a call when read on 2026-10-04 [2274](#cite:2274) [2349](#cite:2349). Community foundations use the same form: Silicon Valley Community Foundation ran its Community Action Grants by a request for proposals open from March 2 to March 31, 2026 [2412](#cite:2412).

short: A rule under which a person cannot apply directly for an award: the institution puts the candidate forward, and the funder caps how many it may name.
definition: An arrangement in which a candidate for an award cannot apply directly and is put forward by the institution, or by a named officer of it, under a cap the funder sets, so that the institution chooses among its own faculty before the funder sees anything [2174](#cite:2174) [2175](#cite:2175). The cap and the nominator are set on each programme page [2146](#cite:2146) [2206](#cite:2206) [2149](#cite:2149). For the 2027 Pew Scholars award one nominee is invited from each of 212 participating institutions, and for the 2026 Packard Fellowships the president of each of 50 invited institutions may make up to two nominations [2174](#cite:2174) [2149](#cite:2149). Some fellowships are closed to all but a list of institutions the funder has chosen, and none of the pages read gives a way for an institution to ask to be added [2149](#cite:2149) [2174](#cite:2174) [2212](#cite:2212). A federal case: NEH's Summer Stipends page states that institutions may nominate only one faculty member at a deadline [989](#cite:989).

short: A request for money that the funder did not invite. A private foundation states on its annual return whether it accepts such requests.
definition: A proposal or request for funds that a foundation has not invited; whether a private foundation accepts such requests is stated on its Form 990-PF, at Part XIV, line 2, which opens with a check box [2387](#cite:2387). The box reads "Check here if the foundation only makes contributions to preselected charitable organizations and does not accept unsolicited requests for funds." [2387](#cite:2387) A foundation that leaves it unchecked fills in lines 2a to 2d with the contact, the form of application, the deadlines and the restrictions; the entry is the foundation's own statement for the tax year of the return, and its website may say something newer [2387](#cite:2387). Public charities such as community foundations file Form 990 and have no such line [2374](#cite:2374). Packard reports that less than one percent of its grants come from unsolicited proposals [2283](#cite:2283).

short: A grant that pays for an organisation's work as a whole and is not tied to one project.
definition: A grant that pays for an organisation's work as a whole [2261](#cite:2261). Ford defines it as funds for day-to-day work, often as multi-year commitments, and Open Society as support "that cover the day-to-day costs of operations" [2261](#cite:2261) [2293](#cite:2293). Foundations differ on it: Hewlett says it "Provides long-term, general operating support whenever possible", while Woodruff says most of its grants support one-time needs [2280](#cite:2280) [2313](#cite:2313). Ford reported in November 2022 that 81% of its grantmaking was general or core support, up from 36% [2333](#cite:2333). The kind of grant can decide the indirect cost rule: Ford's and MacArthur's indirect cost rates apply to project grants and not to general operating support [2332](#cite:2332) [2265](#cite:2265).

short: A foundation grant that pays for one named piece of work with its own budget, as distinct from support for the organisation as a whole.
definition: A foundation grant that pays for one named piece of work with its own budget; foundations also call it project support, and it is one of the two main kinds of foundation grant, the other being general operating support [2261](#cite:2261). Ford describes project support as funds for distinct initiatives that are "usually time-bound, and aimed at achieving specific goals" [2261](#cite:2261). Some funders prefer it: Woodruff says "Most grants support one-time needs rather than ongoing program or operating needs" [2313](#cite:2313). Ford's and MacArthur's indirect cost rates apply to project grants and not to general operating support [2332](#cite:2332) [2265](#cite:2265). The term here is not NIH's "research project grants", which NIH's budget documents count among its own awards [57](#cite:57).

short: The application an organisation files with the IRS to be recognised as tax-exempt under section 501(c)(3). Form 1023-EZ is a shorter version open only to small organisations.
definition: The application on which an organisation asks the IRS to recognise it as exempt under section 501(c)(3), a step separate from becoming a non-profit under state law; Form 1023-EZ is the shorter version [2046](#cite:2046) [2049](#cite:2049) [2047](#cite:2047). The short form is open only to an organisation that answers "No" to every question on its eligibility worksheet, whose first questions ask whether annual gross receipts exceed $50,000 and whether total assets have a fair market value above $250,000 [2050](#cite:2050). Supporting organisations and private operating foundations are among those that cannot use it [2050](#cite:2050). Both are completed on Pay.gov, where the user fee is paid: $600 for Form 1023 and $275 for Form 1023-EZ [2046](#cite:2046) [2049](#cite:2049) [2051](#cite:2051). The IRS says it issues 80% of Form 1023-EZ determinations within 22 days and 80% of Form 1023 determinations within 191 days, on a page last updated June 28, 2026 [2053](#cite:2053).

short: The letter in which the IRS says it has recognised an organisation as tax-exempt. Funders look it up to check a non-profit's standing.
definition: The letter the IRS issues on an application for recognition of tax exemption; section 501(c)(3) status is decided by it [2059](#cite:2059) [2046](#cite:2046). Determination letters can be looked up in the IRS Tax Exempt Organization Search, the tool in which a funder checks a non-profit, and the IRS warns of delays in that tool's data [2059](#cite:2059). The IRS says it issues 80% of Form 1023-EZ determinations within 22 days and 80% of Form 1023 determinations within 191 days, on a page last updated June 28, 2026 [2053](#cite:2053). A subordinate covered by a central organisation's group exemption letter holds the status without its own application [2060](#cite:2060). An organisation asked for proof of status can also request an affirmation letter from the IRS [2066](#cite:2066).

short: Loss of tax-exempt status that follows of itself when an organisation files no annual return or notice for three years in a row.
definition: The loss of tax-exempt status that follows of itself when an exempt organisation files no annual return or notice for three consecutive years; it takes effect on the original filing due date of the third return or notice [2057](#cite:2057). The organisation is removed from the IRS list of organisations eligible for deductible contributions and appears on the Automatic Revocation List, which a funder will find in the Tax Exempt Organization Search [2057](#cite:2057) [2059](#cite:2059). A revoked organisation must apply again, with the user fee, by one of four procedures in Revenue Procedure 2014-11 [2058](#cite:2058). One that was eligible to file Form 990-EZ or 990-N and has not been revoked before may use streamlined retroactive reinstatement if it applies within 15 months [2058](#cite:2058). Others may seek retroactive reinstatement with a statement of reasonable cause, or be reinstated from the post-mark date of the new application [2058](#cite:2058).

short: An IRS letter to a central organisation that also recognises the organisations under its supervision as tax-exempt, so that they do not apply one by one.
definition: A letter by which the IRS recognises as exempt the subordinate organisations under a central organisation's general supervision or control; a subordinate included in the letter does not file its own application [2060](#cite:2060). Subordinates must all be described in the same paragraph of section 501(c), and a central organisation needs at least five subordinates to obtain a letter and at least one to keep it [2060](#cite:2060). The procedure changed in 2026: Revenue Procedure 2026-8, effective January 20, 2026, superseded Revenue Procedure 80-27, and the IRS resumed accepting group applications after that date [2060](#cite:2060) [2061](#cite:2061). As the bulletin was returned when read, section 501(c)(3) subordinates must be public charities with the same foundation classification [2061](#cite:2061). The IRS pages read do not say how a funder verifies that a particular subordinate is covered [2060](#cite:2060).

short: The steps a private foundation must take when it funds an organisation that is not a public charity, to see that the grant is spent for its purpose and to report on it to the IRS.
definition: The duty a private foundation takes on when it makes a grant to an organisation that is not a public charity: to make all reasonable efforts and set up procedures to see that the grant is spent only for its purpose, to get full reports from the grantee, and to report in detail to the IRS [2381](#cite:2381). Without it such a grant is a taxable expenditure under section 4945, while a grant to a public charity needs none of these steps [2380](#cite:2380). For this purpose grants include loans and program-related investments [2380](#cite:2380). Walmart's page gives the foreign case: an organisation outside the United States must show equivalency to a public charity or be funded under expenditure responsibility [2433](#cite:2433). Some funders require public charity status outright: the Bank of America Charitable Foundation requires applicants to be "not classified as a private foundation" [2439](#cite:2439).

short: A draft regulation that an agency publishes in the Federal Register for public comment. It applies to no one until a final rule is published and takes effect.
definition: A draft of a regulation that an agency publishes in the Federal Register and opens to public comment, also called a notice of proposed rulemaking or NPRM; until it is finalised it applies to no one [1858](#cite:1858) [1480](#cite:1480) [1803](#cite:1803). The case this guide follows is OMB's "Regulation for Federal Financial Assistance", a proposal to revise the government-wide grant rules that include the Uniform Guidance, published May 29, 2026 at 91 FR 32198 with comments due on or before July 13, 2026 [1858](#cite:1858) [1803](#cite:1803). The Federal Register record shows 496,606 comments, and OMB's regulatory agenda of August 14, 2026 lists the rule in the proposed rule stage with no date for final action [1858](#cite:1858) [1859](#cite:1859). Section 157 of Public Law 119-103 bars a rule arising from it from being issued or finalised through December 11, 2026, and the Uniform Guidance as revised in 2024 remains the rule in force [1480](#cite:1480) [1857](#cite:1857) [1801](#cite:1801).

short: A regulation in its adopted form, published in the Federal Register with the date on which it takes effect.
definition: The document, published in the Federal Register, by which an agency adopts or changes a regulation and states when it takes effect [2096](#cite:2096) [2008](#cite:2008). The Department of Energy's final rule on conflict of interest policies was published July 16, 2026 at 91 FR 43511 and took effect August 17, 2026, when it superseded an interim policy [2096](#cite:2096). A rule can be in effect before all of it applies: the HHS final rule revising 42 CFR part 93 on research misconduct was published September 17, 2024, was effective January 1, 2025, and all of its requirements apply on or after January 1, 2026 [2008](#cite:2008). A proposed rule is an earlier stage: when the Federal Register record was read on 2026-10-04, no final rule had followed OMB's proposal of May 29, 2026 to revise the Uniform Guidance, and Public Law 119-103 bars one through December 11, 2026 [1858](#cite:1858) [1480](#cite:1480).

short: A numbered presidential order that directs federal agencies, published in the Federal Register. It tells agencies what to do and does not itself rewrite a regulation.
definition: A numbered presidential document, signed and then published in the Federal Register, that directs federal agencies to act [246](#cite:246) [2097](#cite:2097). Executive Order 14332, signed August 7, 2025 and published at 90 FR 38929, requires a senior appointee's review of new funding announcements and discretionary awards and directs OMB to revise the Uniform Guidance [246](#cite:246). Its section 7 says that the order creates no enforceable rights and is to be implemented consistent with applicable law [246](#cite:246). The revision it directs was published as a proposed rule on May 29, 2026 and had not been finalised on 2026-10-04; Public Law 119-103 bars a final rule through December 11, 2026 [1803](#cite:1803) [1858](#cite:1858) [1480](#cite:1480). Steps taken under an order can be challenged in court: a district court vacated the actions that implemented Executive Order 14238 at the Institute of Museum and Library Services [688](#cite:688) [687](#cite:687).

short: A court order that bars an agency from carrying out or enforcing a policy or action. It protects the parties the order names.
definition: A court order that bars an agency from carrying out or enforcing a policy or action [24](#cite:24) [1479](#cite:1479). In the cases this guide records a preliminary injunction comes early in a suit and a permanent one with the judgment: a district court enjoined NIH's notice of a 15 percent indirect cost rate on March 5, 2025, later made the injunction permanent and vacated the notice, and the First Circuit affirmed on January 5, 2026 [24](#cite:24). A court order protects only the parties and classes it names; the order of September 21, 2026 against five departments' notices on public benefits bars enforcement against the plaintiff states and the District of Columbia [1867](#cite:1867) [1879](#cite:1879) [1479](#cite:1479). An injunction can itself be undone on appeal: on February 6, 2026 the Fourth Circuit vacated a nationwide preliminary injunction against provisions of Executive Orders 14151 and 14173 [1865](#cite:1865).

short: A court's cancelling of an agency policy, notice or decision, so that it is no longer in effect. Court orders also say that the action is set aside.
definition: A court's cancelling of an agency policy, notice or decision; the orders pair the words, as in "The PRWORA Notices are declared unlawful under the APA and ordered set aside and vacated." [1479](#cite:1479) The District of Massachusetts vacated NSF's 15 percent indirect cost policy on June 20, 2025, and NSF states that the policy is not in effect [238](#cite:238) [237](#cite:237) [154](#cite:154). It is a separate remedy from an injunction: on August 7, 2026 the District of Rhode Island set aside HUD's fiscal year 2026 Continuum of Care notice in its entirety and denied a permanent injunction [1478](#cite:1478). A vacatur can be paused, as when the First Circuit stayed that ruling pending appeal on September 16, 2026 [1283](#cite:1283). A court may grant neither, as in the declaratory judgment of July 17, 2026 in New Jersey v. OMB [1869](#cite:1869).

short: The state of a court ruling that a party has taken to a higher court. The ruling may stay in force or be paused, by a stay, while the appeal runs.
definition: The state of a court ruling that a party has asked a higher court to review; whether the ruling is in force meanwhile turns on a stay pending appeal, an order that pauses it while the appeal proceeds [30](#cite:30) [543](#cite:543) [1283](#cite:1283). The First Circuit denied one on September 17, 2025 in State of New York v. Kennedy, which left the district court's injunction of July 1, 2025 in place [543](#cite:543). It granted one on September 16, 2026 against the ruling that vacated HUD's fiscal year 2026 Continuum of Care notice, and HUD reopened the notice on September 18, 2026 [1283](#cite:1283). On August 21, 2025 the Supreme Court did both in one order: it stayed the judgments vacating NIH grant terminations and left in place the vacatur of the guidance documents [28](#cite:28). Orders on stay applications are not final rulings on the merits [1804](#cite:1804) [28](#cite:28).

short: A law in which Congress provides money to federal agencies for a fiscal year. It can also carry conditions on how grant money is used.
definition: A law in which Congress provides money for federal agencies and their programmes for a fiscal year [173](#cite:173) [1480](#cite:1480). Fiscal year 2026 was funded by twelve appropriations acts, among them the Consolidated Appropriations Act, 2026 (Public Law 119-75), signed February 3, 2026 [1480](#cite:1480) [21](#cite:21). An act carries conditions as well as amounts: section 224 of that law keeps the indirect cost provisions of 45 CFR part 75 applying to NIH grants, and Congress may also name a specific recipient, project and amount in an act [62](#cite:62) [1667](#cite:1667) [1674](#cite:1674). The amounts are set by Congress and can differ from the President's request: for NSF's Graduate Research Fellowship Program in fiscal year 2026 the request was $127.3 million and a society summary reports $285 million in the final bill [884](#cite:884) [174](#cite:174). Award amounts and new competitions for fiscal year 2027 depend on acts not yet enacted on 2026-10-04 [1480](#cite:1480).

short: A stopgap law that keeps agencies funded at a set rate for a limited time when a fiscal year starts without full-year appropriations.
definition: A law that keeps agencies funded at a set rate for a limited time when a fiscal year starts without full-year appropriations; under one, agencies keep operating and keep making awards, with limits on how much and how fast [1480](#cite:1480) [1874](#cite:1874). Fiscal year 2027 began on October 1, 2026 under Public Law 119-103, approved September 2, 2026, which continues the fiscal year 2026 acts through December 11, 2026 or the earlier enactment of an appropriation [1480](#cite:1480) [83](#cite:83). Its section 104 bars starting a project or activity for which funds were not available in fiscal year 2026, and section 109 says no grants shall be awarded that would impinge on final funding prerogatives [1480](#cite:1480). NIH states that its institutes may issue non-competing awards below the level on the most recent Notice of Award [83](#cite:83). When neither a full-year act nor a resolution is in force, appropriations lapse and an agency does not process new awards [1875](#cite:1875) [1872](#cite:1872).

short: What the President asks Congress to provide for an agency in the coming fiscal year. It is a proposal; the amounts are set by the appropriations acts.
definition: The administration's proposal of amounts for an agency for the coming fiscal year, sent with estimates and justifications to the Senate and House appropriations committees [59](#cite:59) [57](#cite:57). It is a request and not law, and this guide records every budget request as proposed: award amounts and new competitions depend on the appropriations acts [1480](#cite:1480). The fiscal year 2027 President's Budget requests $41.5 billion for NIH at programme level and proposes a 15 percent cap on F&A costs for each award [57]. A request and the outcome can differ: for NSF's Graduate Research Fellowship Program in fiscal year 2026 the request was $127.3 million, and a society summary reports $285 million in the final bill [884](#cite:884) [174](#cite:174). No enacted fiscal year 2027 appropriations act had been found when the sources were read on 2026-10-04 [1873](#cite:1873).

short: The cancelling of something already in place. Congress rescinds money it had appropriated; an agency rescinds a notice or an award term it had issued.
definition: A cancelling of something already in place, met in two forms in this guide's records. Congress can take back money it has appropriated: the Rescissions Act of 2025 (Public Law 119-28), approved July 24, 2025, rescinded the amounts made available for the Corporation for Public Broadcasting for fiscal years 2026 and 2027, and the Corporation announced a wind-down on August 1, 2025 [1407](#cite:1407) [1406](#cite:1406). An agency can also withdraw its own notice or award term. The Rural Housing Service rescinded the fiscal year 2025 Rural Community Development Initiative notice on July 2, 2026; applications already submitted do not advance, and a new application is needed under a future notice [1412](#cite:1412). NIH rescinded on June 12, 2025 a civil rights term of award that it had added on April 21, 2025 [1870](#cite:1870) [1871](#cite:1871).

short: This guide's label for a change that has been signed, announced or enacted but has not yet taken effect or been carried out in full.
definition: A label of this guide's own on a record of change; it is not a legal term. It marks a change that has been signed, announced or enacted and whose effect lies ahead, or whose carrying-out is unfinished. Records so marked include an NIH notice of July 27, 2026 that replaces letters of support with letters of collaboration from fiscal year 2027 [131](#cite:131), Executive Order 14332 of August 7, 2025, whose directed revision of the Uniform Guidance has not been made final [246](#cite:246) [1480](#cite:1480), and the Department of Education's interagency agreements announced November 18, 2025 [672](#cite:672). The label says nothing about whether the change will arrive on the date given. The other labels on records of change are proposed, announced, enacted, final, enjoined, vacated, in-litigation, on-appeal, rescinded and frozen-by-appropriations.

short: The one-word label this guide puts on each programme record to say where its competition stood on the day the funder's pages were read.
definition: A label of this guide's own on every programme record, saying where the programme's competition stood on the day its pages were read; each record carries that date. The labels are: open (a notice is in force and takes applications, or its next due date is still ahead); forecast (no open notice, and a forecast or an announced date for the next one); closed (the last deadline has passed and the funder's page shows the programme continuing); expired (the announcement lapsed, was archived or was ended early, and nothing replaces it); not-competed; no-current-notice; formula (money allotted by formula or block grant, with no federal competition a non-profit can enter); and unconfirmed (the pages would not load or do not settle the question). A programme with several notices takes the status of the notice a new applicant would use. A status is a reading on one day and goes out of date quickly.

short: This guide's label for a programme with no notice for the current cycle and no statement from the funder that it has ended. It reports an absence, not a closure.
definition: A label of this guide's own. It marks a programme record for which no notice for the current cycle was found on the funder's page or on Grants.gov, while the funder has not said that the programme has ended. It reports an absence on the day of reading, with the listing cited in the record, and does not say that the programme is over or that a notice is coming. One record so marked rests on a programme page that states "There are no open NOFOs at this time" and gives no date for a next solicitation and no statement that the programme has ended [312](#cite:312). Where the funder has said that a competition is cancelled or will not be held, the label is not-competed; where a forecast exists, it is forecast.

short: This guide's label for a programme whose funder has said that the competition is cancelled, paused or will not be held.
definition: A label of this guide's own. It marks a programme record whose funder has said that the competition is cancelled, paused or will not be held. It differs from no-current-notice, which records only that no notice was found, and from closed, where a deadline has passed and the programme continues. One record so marked is the Social Security Administration's Retirement and Disability Research Consortium: the agency's release of February 21, 2025 states that it terminated the consortium's cooperative agreements [626](#cite:626). The label reports what the funder had said when its pages were read and does not say whether a competition will return.
